Luxury automaker Mercedes-Benz is halting investment at its facilities in Germany, a board members announced on Thursday.

Mercedes-Benz is "forced to examine, in concrete and detailed terms, which sites in Germany we can still afford to maintain," board of management member Britta Seeger said in an interview published on the company's intranet.

Germany's major IG Metall trade union has enabled the possibility of longer warning strikes amid difficult negotiations for industrial employees.

"The board of IG Metall has pave the way for 24-hour warning strikes in the metalworking and electrical industry," the union said on Thursday.

The union accuses employers of intransigence after three rounds of negotiations without clear progress.

On Wednesday, regional chapters appealed for authorization for full-day warning strikes — the last step before a full union vote and an indefinite labor dispute.

Sources indicate that "This escalation is completely excessive and counterproductive," Udo Dinglreiter, the president of the employers' umbrella organization, Gesamtmetall, said. He said that hundreds of thousands of jobs could be at risk.

IG Metall's first chairperson Christiane Benner countered that "the employers want to turn this round of collective bargaining into a dispute over principles." Another union official said they were offering what amounted to a real-terms pay cut rather than seeking solutions.

IG Metall is calling for a 5% pay increase and other improved conditions for some 3.7 million workers starting in November, while employers have offered a one-off payment in 2027 coupled with a 1.3% increase starting in the summer of 2028.

The union estimates that around 464,000 employees took part in the initial wave of warning strikes that were limited to periods of hours, rather than full days.

Employers argue that they're treading a difficult line between trying not to cut jobs and meeting calls for improved pay amid widespread industrial sector layoffs in Germany in recent years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, 'Tis the season, already. Preparations are underway around Germany and in several cities, Christmas markets are opening to the public.

Some markets are already open in Essen and in Hamburg, Duisburg's opens on Thursday, and Cologne's follows a day later.

The coupons.de website has sought to track the planned prices for mulled wine or Glühwein as the markets open their doors nationwide.

According to recent reports, the bad news? These prices are rising like so many others. The better news? The year-on-year increase is actually smaller than overall inflation figures, at around 1%.

On average, a cup is liable to set you back around €4.60 (roughly $5.10). Not entirely surprisingly, Munich tops the nationwide pricing chart, with the price peaking at €7. Other sites nationwide tend not to have the gall even to charge 6 euros.

Bargain hunters determined to get the best value mulled wine will need to venture deep into the center of Germany — hardly its core tourist hub — to find the lowest prices starting at around €3.50.

Deposits for the cup, the "Pfand," are also only going in one direction, and in the meantime range from €1 all the way up to €5. But there's a strong argument, particularly with the better designs or after a memorable trip, that this can be money well spent as a memento!

Police in the Emsland region in the northwest near the border to the Netherlands have reported a major fire in a complex of residential and commercial buildings in Papenburg.

The fire broke out on Wednesday afternoon, police said the following morning, causing damages worth "at least €10 million ($11 million)." Several hundred emergency services personnel were deployed.

"Based on current findings, the fire broke out in the sauna area of a gym facility on site, and swiftly spread to further parts of the complex of buildings," police wrote.

Two men were in the sauna at the time and initially tried to douse the flames but without success.

Police remarked the buildings were evacuated as the fire spread, with some surrounding buildings also being cleared as a precaution because of possible smoke-related dangers.

Several people were injured, police stated, including the two men in the sauna area suffering mild burns and suspected smoke inhalation sickness. They were treated in a nearby hospital but soon discharged.

Recent findings suggest that "There were also injuries among the first responders," police wrote. "Four police officers, two firefighters and members of the rescue teams suffered mild injuries, particularly via smoke inhalation.".

The fire was only extinguished late on Wednesday night, several hours after it started. The area is sealed off, with possible risks of damaged buildings collapsing. Police have also rolled out investigations into the fire's cause, but remarked that at present, the area was not safe for that work to start at full scale.

Germany's largest credit bureau Creditreform has published its "2026 Debtors' Atlas.".

It finds that 10.16% of German adults, or 7.36 million people, exhibit at least the early warning signs of excessive debt. A year ago the ratio was 9.74%.

"The financial situation of private consumers has further deteriorated," Patrik-Ludwig Hantzsch, Creditreform's head of economic research, said. "In particular, the sharply increased living costs, energy costs and housing costs are straining expenditures.".

Hantzsch remarked employment was also becoming an concern once more, saying "above all, well-paid jobs in manufacturing industries have been cut back in large numbers in recent months.".

The report also highlights rising cases of signs of excessive debt prior to legal action being taken, such as payment reminders or warnings being sent, saying "consumers are taking on more credit-financed expenditures — increasingly also for smaller purchases — at simultaneously rising interest rates.".

A larger share of men than women have excessive debts, perpetuating a longstanding trend.

People around the middle of their working lives, aged 30-39 and 40-49, are most likely to be affected — but the cohort with the fastest-rising share of people with excessive debts are young adults below the age of 30.

Bremen, Berlin, Saxony-Anhalt and North Rhine-Westphalia were among the states with the highest rates of excess debts, while the wealthy and fiscally conservative states of Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg had the lowest levels.

Germany's main DAX stock market index has cleared the 27,000-point mark for the first time in its history in morning trading.

It climbed by around 1.3% in order to pass the milestone.

A combination of some positive outlook data from major companies, not least engineering giant Siemens, and the falling oil prices of recent days have helped fuel the uptick.

Siemens' shares had risen by almost 5%, to just over €291 (around $323) each, helping to spur on the gains and making the company the morning's top performer.

Despite several years of low growth and recession in the German economy, the DAX, like many Western indices, is now trading twice as high as it was prior to the COVID pandemic.

Hundreds of police officers searched apartments and meeting sites for the biker group "Gremium MC" in the southwestern state of Baden-Württemberg early on Thursday.

The state interior ministry said the operation was part of a move to outlaw three sub-chapters of the group, the ones based in Böblingen and Leonberg, as well as the "Gremium MC Chapter Nomads Bosphorus Türkiye.".

According to recent reports, this last group was highlighted as a meaningful part of Gremium MC by security officials. It describes itself on Facebook as a great example that "people of different cultures and faiths can be strong together," featuring images of men posing with knives and other weapons.

Gremium MC prominently incorporates into its iconography the symbol of the Prussian military medal for exceptional valor, the Iron Cross, which was discontinued after World War I, reintroduced by Adolf Hitler during World War II, and then scrapped for good.

State Interior Minister Manuel Hagel was expected to make further comments later in the day in Ludwigsburg.

Gremium MC is deemed an "outlaw motorcycle gang" in Baden-Württemberg's latest security report, a term used for biker groups that do not recognize the state monopoly on the use of force and are often tied to organized crime.

"Extortion, drug dealing and pimping in particular tend to be part of their activities," state authorities say.

Baden-Württemberg counts 154 biker chapters in the state with around 2,000 members.

Industry observers note that founded in 1972 in Mannheim, various chapters of Gremium MC across the country have faced legal concerns in recent years. In 2021, another chapter in the southwest, Gremium MC Southgate in Heidelberg, was outlawed on suspicion of organized crime activity.

Police in Hanover reported early on Thursday that three men were injured by an unknown driver in a car in the nearby town of Ronneberg.

One person sustained severe injuries in the incident late on Wednesday, police stated.

Two of the wounded were taken to a nearby hospital while the other could be cared for at the scene.

It has been revealed that police noted the driver fled the scene and that a search operation was ongoing. Authorities were also still investigating a potential motive for the apparent attack.

Today's updates start with a focus between the southwestern Kurpfalz and Swabian regions, where police have released major morning raids against a biker gang.

Sources indicate that the state Interior Ministry in Baden Württemberg has outlawed three of its chapters. Hundreds of police officers mobilized in the early hours of the morning.

The major IG Metall trade union is planning further strikes in the carmaking sector and other metalworking industries, with an announcement anticipated later in the day.

To the north, near Hanover, police report an apparent car attack injuring three men overnight.

Sources indicate that and in the spirit of offering the public service journalism people are truly thirsting for, we'll have some info on the average and localized pricing of mulled wine or Glühwein at Christmas markets this year, as the early birds start to open their doors to visitors. (Yes, already!).

Stay tuned for updates on all this and anything else of note in or pertaining to Germany as the day progresses.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nick Woltemade had an immediate impact for Juventus, helping the Bianconeri secure a 4-0 home win over struggling Venezia with one goal and one assist after coming on from the bench.

Juventus beat Venezia 4-0 in Turin on Sunday, scoring all four goals in the second half.

See how the game unfolded on the live blog.

Edon Zhegrova was the significant surprise in the Juventus XI as the Kosovo international started a Serie A match for the first time in his career. The ex-Lille star was arguably the most dangerous Juventus player in the first half, but Venezia had the best chances before the break.

Recent findings suggest that the first clear chance fell to summer signing Akor Adams. Just five minutes in, the striker found plenty of space after receiving the ball just behind the halfway line and drove towards Guglielmo Vicario’s goal. However, a heavy touch as he prepared to shoot allowed Gleison Bremer to recover, with the Juventus defender tracking back brilliantly to block Adams’ effort.

Sources indicate that zhegrova had a good chance a few minutes later, nutmegging USMNT international Gianluca Busio on the left flank and trying to score with a curler at the near post, but Filip Stankovic saved it. Busio later earned a corner kick for Venezia when Vicario deflected his shot from distance.

Juventus’ best chance came in the final minute of the first half, when Weston McKennie headed a Douglas Luiz corner kick from the left, but didn’t find the target.

Juventus were booed by their fans when the referee blew the half-time whistle, but it triggered the team’s reaction after the break.

Nick Woltemade was introduced to replace the injured Kerim Alajbegovic, and the Newcastle loanee made an immediate impact, scoring and assisting in 15 minutes.

The German broke the deadlock in the 53rd minute, pouncing on a McKennie shot deflected by Juan Jesus inside the box and beating the onrushing Filip Stankovic to score his second consecutive goal in Serie A.

Just five minutes later, Teun Koopmeiners won the ball high up the pitch, linked up with Woltemade inside the box and found the net with a curler at the far post.

In a recent development, juventus’ two goals entirely changed the energy inside the Allianz Stadium. Juan Cabal scored the third goal for the home side, outjumping the Venezia defence from a short corner performed by Koopmeiners and Zhegrova.

In a recent development, five minutes later, Randal Kolo Muani earned a penalty by outsprinting Halhal on the left flank; the Venezia defender slid in inside the box, but didn’t get the ball. Woltemade took the ball in his hand and seemed ready to take the spot-kick, but then gave it to Kolo Muani, who scored his second Serie A goal this season.

Venezia had one final chance when John Yeboah struck the crossbar with a curler from the edge of the box, but Juventus had already put the game to bed.

The victory allows the Old Lady to climb to sixth, still five points below fourth-placed Como, their next opponent in Serie A.

Meanwhile, Venezia remain 19th with just six points from 12 matches and one win in their last five.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that towards the end of their lives, stars experience a drastic change in their structure as they swell and enter what is known as their giant phase. Because most stars are thought to host orbiting companions (such as planets, other stars or black holes), interesting interactions can happen as the giant host expands. The most striking of these occur when a companion star is engulfed by a giant: astronomers refer to this as the common-envelope phase1. Despite theoretical expectations that common envelopes should be widespread in stellar evolution, they have been extraordinarily difficult to observe. Writing in Nature, however, Karambelkar et al.2 report the first direct detection of a star inside a giant star.

According to TEAMtalk, Inter are preparing for significant changes in defence and have placed Mosquera high on their shortlist ahead of the summer transfer window.

The Serie A giants were interested in him before his £13million move from Valencia to Arsenal in 2025 and have continued monitoring his development.

Mosquera’s lack of minutes understandably creates questions about his long-term future, but Arsenal should resist making a premature decision.

Rangers must find their shooting boots quicker to prevent the need to dig themselves out of needless holes

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.
  • He wants to place the focus, instead, on a 13-game unbeaten run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026.

Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.

That’s fair enough. He wants to keep the energy up. He wants to place the focus, instead, on a 13-game unbeaten run. He wants to make more of the fact his team are capable of digging in and getting wins over the line by hook or by crook even when it isn’t going exactly to initiative.

It’s a form of motivation, and motivating people doesn’t always come through hammering on about their deficiencies. The truth is this, though: you really shouldn’t be needing a scrappy 88th-minute winner courtesy of a couple of jammy deflections in a game which has seen you deliver 29 shots on goal with 11 of those on target.

It has been revealed that yes, Motherwell keeper Alex Paulsen had a good night. One double save from substitute Findlay Curtis and Dujon Sterling in the 85th minute was quite exceptional. This, however, wasn’t quite the superhuman display from the Kiwi that many were making it out to be.

A lot of the saves he made were straightforward. Too often, Rangers blazed efforts high and wide. They dominated the first quarter of this game until Jake Girdwood-Reich cancelled out Manny Fernandez’s early opener, lost their rhythm a bit, as they are wont to do, and then ran the show completely in the second half.

They should have won by a country mile and it is necessary to look into why they didn’t.

Ryan Naderi rejoices in scoring Rangers' late winner against Motherwell.

Emmanuel Fernandez broke the deadlock on eight minutes at Fir Park.

Industry observers note that mcInnes was justified in being happy with many aspects of his side’s performance at Fir Park. Ryan Naderi did put in a strong display as he spearheaded the frontline, although he did miss two gilt-edged chances before settling it late on with an untidy effort that deflected off Martin Moormann — who had already blocked a Badredine Bouanani shot — and landed in the net.

The Czech international is developing a reputation for key goals that are getting Rangers out of the mire — and keeping them in contention for the title — but McInnes needs infinitely more in terms of numbers from those around him.

It has been revealed that not xG or pass completion or any of those niche interests. Goals and assists is what we’re talking about here. The stuff that really changes games and puts points on the board.

First in the dock on this front, talented individuals that really need to be held to account, are attackers Minsu Kim and Bouanani. Listen, McInnes has already spoken plenty on the need for both of them to deliver more in those key metrics. He obviously doesn’t want to come across as a stuck record.

Both players are technically proficient. They are exciting. The view from this vantage point is that they very definitely do have it in them to be gamechangers, but they’re starting to get a little bit annoying now.

In a recent development, thanks to the corner that set up Fernandez for the opening goal, Minsu, who started in a more central role with Kevin Kelsy being benched, does have one assist on the board finally. That’s a pretty grim return, though, from 15 appearances.

According to recent reports, particularly worrying from the South Korean was his reaction when presented with a golden opportunity to break his scoring duck just before the hour. Naderi teed him up perfectly with a pass to the left. Minsu had time to control the ball and pick his spot.

According to recent reports, his sclaffed effort, easily saved by Paulsen at the near post, was atrocious. It reeked of a guy short of confidence in the final third and growing progressively more anxious about getting his name on the scoresheet. Maybe he’s just trying too hard, but he needs to get the finger out, keep the mind calm and start taking the heat off the likes of Naderi and Kelsy with some major contributions.

Same goes for Bouanani. His late effort did, at least, lead to Naderi’s winner, albeit more through accident than design, but his record reads one goal and one assist in 10 appearances. He’s a dangerous, tricky winger. He beats people for fun. He should be doing more than this.

Djeidi Gassama, a more limited player than Minsu or Bouanani, started against Motherwell and does have five assists to his name, but he’s only managed one goal, in a 5-1 League Cup rout of St Mirren.

Meanwhile, Findlay Curtis has no goals and no assists from 15 outings, although only five of those have been first-team starts.

That’s four blokes who play along the frontline and they’ve managed two goals between them. You do the maths on that.

Derek McInnes was delighted at full-time but Rangers should have won with more comfort.

There are others throughout the team, though, who can be doing more to make life easier from a goalscoring perspective.

Fernandez declared himself as a real threat from set-pieces last season. He’s a real weapon in the air. Saturday’s goal was his first this term. Rangers need to do better at harnessing what he brings in an attacking context from dead-ball situations.

A few more in the way of goal interventions from midfield would be welcome, too. Dan Neil can finish. He demonstrated that with those two spectacular goals against Celtic in the 3-0 Premier Sports Cup win at Ibrox in September.

In his 17 other outings outwith that match, however, he has only scored once and delivered one assist. He had a brilliant chance at Fir Park just after the interval and slid it wide of the far post.

Nico Raskin, meanwhile, has one goal and no assists to his name.

Sources indicate that he put one great chance from a header wide in the second half. Then he blazed over from a promising position after releasing Bouanani out wide with a super diagonal ball and running a ridiculous distance to latch onto the return.

McInnes insists he’s never seen a squad practise crossing and shooting like this one. However much they are doing in training at Auchenhowie, they need to bring it to matchdays.

Industry observers note that everything is there for Rangers this season. There are definitely promising signs in their overall play while Celtic, of course, are poorly run from a footballing perspective with an OAP manager, and a fanbase in open revolt against the board.

Rangers now have a run of six games from eight at home that could — and should — be a real platform for a serious title bid.

They just have to wake up to the fact that depending on Naderi to drag them out of a hole and drag them over the line again and again and again is simply not a sustainable way of working.

#60154. What are fossil fuels?

What are fossil fuels?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (607 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, whether in the form of crumbly rock, odorless gas or slick black liquid, ancient organic compounds have powered the flourishing of modern life.
  • The collective term refers to coal, oil and natural gas — a group of energy sources that contain carbon and hydrogen.
  • They started life hundreds of millions of years ago as living plants and animals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, whether in the form of crumbly rock, odorless gas or slick black liquid, ancient organic compounds have powered the flourishing of modern life. But now they threaten to make the planet unlivable for many plants, animals and humans.

The collective term refers to coal, oil and natural gas — a group of energy sources that contain carbon and hydrogen.

They started life hundreds of millions of years ago as living plants and animals. When they died, they sank to the bottom of oceans and swamps where they decomposed under layers of sediment.

In a recent development, over time, this matter was buried deeper and deeper into the earth, subjecting it to increasing pressure and heat which changed its chemical composition. Plants and trees transformed into coal, whereas microscopic plankton and algae became oil and — if the heat and pressure increased further — gas.

Today fossil fuels can be found in the earth's crust all around the world although some countries, such as the US, Saudi Arabia and Russia, have bigger reserves than others.

Coal, found in underground coal beds, is extracted by mining, whereas oil and gas, found in reservoirs beneath the land and ocean, are accessed by drilling.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Since the early 19th Century, when the discovery and exploitation of fossil fuel reserves powered the Industrial Revolution, our use of them has skyrocketed, increasing eight-fold since 1950.

Today they provide 80% of our energy needs through heating, electricity generation and transport.

According to recent reports, we transform them into energy either by burning them directly in furnaces that warm up our homes and businesses, or in power plants to heat water into steam which then generates electricity. When it comes to transport, crude oil is refined into a range of products such as diesel, gasoline and kerosene that are burned in the engines of automobiles, airplanes and ships. Natural gas is also sometimes compressed for use in cars and buses.

But fossil fuels are also essential to a huge range of products including steel, formed using a coal-derived material called coke, and plastic, which is produced by refining and processing crude oil and gas.

It has been revealed that fossil fuels are by far the biggest contributors to climate change. When burned to power our modern lives, they emit carbon dioxide (CO2) into Earth's atmosphere, trapping heat and causing temperatures to rise.

Sources indicate that with 2025 officially one of the warmest years on record, the impact of these emissions is being felt around the world. Hotter temperatures are causing polar ice caps to melt and creating the conditions for extreme weather events — such as floods, drought, wildfires and storms — to become more intense and frequent.

Scientists stress the need to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) to avoid unleashing the most catastrophic impacts of climate change. That was laid out in the 2015 Paris Agreement. Presently, there are 194 parties to the agreement, but progress has been too slow, and overall emissions continue to rise.

According to recent reports, three years after countries agreed at the UN climate conference in Dubai COP28 to transition away from coal, oil and gas. After the previous COP in Brazil failed to reach a consensus on a concrete strategy, Brazil has now presented a roadmap aimed at turning that promise into national looks.

"It is long past time to stop treating the transition away from fossil fuels as taboo or intractable," United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • After the international break, it’s always difficult to find the rhythm again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nick Woltemade explains why he let his teammate Randal Kolo Muani take a penalty kick in a 4-0 win over Venezia: ‘We both need confidence.’.

Woltemade made an immediate impact, scoring and assisting within 15 minutes of coming off the bench in Juventus’ 4-0 win over Venezia on Sunday.

“It’s an vital win. After the international break, it’s always difficult to find the rhythm again. We knew it was a tough game, but I think we did quite well in the second half and scored at important moments,” Woltemade told DAZN.

Woltemade seemed eager to take the penalty kick from which Juventus scored their fourth goal today, but he gave the ball to Kolo Muani, who didn’t miss his chance and sent Filip Stankovic the wrong way to score this second Serie A goal this season.

“Last time, he gave me the ball; we both need confidence,” Woltemade explained.

According to recent reports, “When we have the chance to help each other, we help each other. I don’t want to act like I’m a good guy who gave him the ball. It was normal for me. He’s a good guy; he took the penalty, and he took it.”.

Woltemade had scored his first Serie A goal in the previous round, just before the break, on an assist from Kolo Muani in a 2-2 away draw at Fiorentina.

Ironically, Woltemade scored his first Juventus goal against NEC in September, when Nico Gonzalez, who was injured today, let him take a penalty kick in a 5-0 Europa League victory.

“It was a gift for me to give me this goal. I’m so happy. He’s my guy,” Kolo Muani said.

“If you play well, I play well, and everyone wins.”.

Juventus had a strong reaction in the second half, going to the break with a 0-0 draw as fans booed the players.

“Of course, we always want to win and give good energy to the fans, but sometimes it takes time to get through and create chances. This is football, and we need to be brave,” concluded Woltemade.

“A game takes 90 minutes; you look at 4-0 and think it was an easy game, but no game is easy. We have quality; we will find solutions.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

David Moyes took a glug of water and glanced up at the big screen away to his right, almost as if he wanted confirmation that what he was seeing was true.

According to recent reports, had he looked behind him, Moyes would have seen Andy Burnham and his wife, Marie-France, in raptures, along with thousands of others. It was true, all right. Everton had scored their third goal and were bounding into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, seemingly without a care in the world.

What a happy change of direction. Moyes has spent months spinning plates, dealing with owners who do not care about a proud club and want to sell up and a squad that was left criminally short in the transfer window. Then, before Newcastle’s visit, came more disruption.

Jack Grealish’s selfish and reckless decision to go Awol from training on Monday could have been a catalyst for more misery and invited Newcastle to deliver a hammer blow to Everton’s season, but again, Moyes fostered a siege mentality. He was rewarded in the most emphatic fashion.

True, Newcastle collapsed like a deckchair without hinges and this performance – which encouraged many of their 8,000 followers to head for the exits early – would not have done anything to convince those who view Matthias Jaissle, the head coach, with ambivalence to change their minds.

In a recent development, the lack of discipline in their ranks was exposed when Dan Burn scored a late consolation and ended up in a melee with James Tarkowski and Joelinton. But the challenges Jaissle, who lamented that “we must improve”, has to correct are for another day: this contest belonged to Everton.

Thierno Barry had provided the finish that secured a trip to Fleetwood in December and what an opportunity it is for Moyes to make Everton semi-finalists in this competition for the first time since 2016. Whether Grealish will have a part to play in it remains to be seen.

It has been revealed that thierno Barry with Everton's third! 🔵 https://t.co/dyb8fKud8N.

The last thing Everton needed on a night of such importance was a distraction. Grealish will have a tough job mending relations, particularly with Moyes, but there was a paradox: though he had caused a major glitch for 90 minutes he became an irrelevance.

Moyes is impatient to give Evertonians a major day out and his only focus was on crossing this hurdle – for all that Newcastle have had a turbulent start to the campaign, they are dangerous opponents and you wondered in the fraught opening 30 minutes if they might exacerbate the hosts’ woes.

As Jaissle hopped and squirmed on the sidelines, imploring Newcastle forward, chances came and went: Harvey Barnes had a header saved, Fabian Schar tested Jordan Pickford from 30 yards while Vitalii Mykolenko and James Tarkowski made huge goal-saving challenges.

Sources indicate that “We should have scored more goals,” Jaissle, who was dressed as if auditioning for the role of The Milk Tray Man, growled. “It [losing] was shocking as the game was not that bad.”.

Moyes was infuriated by Everton’s initial inertia, so much so there was a point when the Scot prevented Merlin Röhl, his own full-back, from taking a throw-in until Tarkowski and Jake O’Brien had complied with his gesturing to get 10 yards further forward.

It might have looked old-fashioned but it worked. Suddenly Everton started asking questions, Hayden Hackney almost got on the end of a cross from Mykolenko, and it encouraged the supporters on the vertiginous South Stand to raise their voices and become more involved.

What they needed was a goal to set things alight and in the 34th minute, it arrived. Tyrique George won possession by Newcastle’s corner flag, the ball dropped at Hackney’s feet and he instinctively ushered it on to James Garner, who whipped a right-footed drive beyond Lukáš Horníček.

James Garner puts Everton in front against Newcastle in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 https://t.co/TzponbWyGU.

The roar that greeted it was a mix of elation and wonder, relief and desperation. The locals have grown weary of seeing nights with potential end in disappointment but here was the foothold they craved and the opportunity they were ready to seize. Soon the lead would be doubled.

Industry observers note that hackney would score the goal, converting a super Barry cross, but let us acknowledge the fabulous refereeing of Farai Hallam, who waved play on when he might have whistled for a foul on Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall. And how Everton took advantage.

Industry observers note that hayden Hackney doubles Everton's advantage! 🔵 https://t.co/VIY0Iln3nI.

Recent findings suggest that it must be noted the officiating this week has, in the main, been outstanding. Watching a match without the persistent spectre of VAR has been liberating and you can see the referees have felt free to make decisions on instinct.

Industry observers note that the whole experience of knowing a contest cannot be re-refereed has been better for all. It will not catch on, sadly, because too many people have gone too far down the road with VAR, but we should embrace the purity of “old school football” while we can.

Evertonians – the Prime Minister included – certainly embraced the buffer of a second goal and the fact Hackney scored it also felt like a throwback: a player who was plucked out of the Championship in the summer and encouraged by Moyes to show he could make the next step up.

It has been revealed that he did that and so, too, did Everton, their progress was assured in the 69th minute when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall dashed down the left and crossed for Barry to finish. Moyes puffed out his cheeks as it hit the net. He, more than most, deserved to enjoy this one.

Speaking exclusively to Sky Sports, Fernandes confirmed United have already made their intentions clear.

“Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.”.

Fernandes’ comments arguably make his position much clearer.

This does not sound like a player simply holding out for a bigger salary. Instead, he appears to want evidence that United can become competitive again before committing the latter stages of his career to Old Trafford.

That puts pressure on Pochettino and the club’s hierarchy.

A recent CaughtOffside report highlighted the uncertainty surrounding Fernandes after his second contract rejection, but United still control the immediate situation because of their extension clause.

Triggering that option should be straightforward if no agreement is reached soon.

The bigger challenge is persuading Fernandes that staying is worthwhile.

Recent findings suggest that at 32, he knows opportunities to join another elite club will not continue indefinitely. United therefore need to show genuine progress rather than simply increase the numbers in a contract proposal.

If Pochettino can swiftly improve performances and restore belief around the club, Fernandes may yet decide that finishing his prime years at Old Trafford is the right choice.

Sky Sports understands Fernandes has rejected two proposals, although United retain the option to extend his contract by another 12 months and protect themselves from losing him for nothing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

English football journalist John Cross has taken on the impossible task of ranking the greatest footballers he's seen in person, and his list of 25 players is bound to cause a debate.

It has been revealed that for any fan, ranking players is a matter of preference, with factors such as playing style, achievements, position and even nationality all coming into play. You'd be hard-pressed to find any Argentine who ranks Cristiano Ronaldo above Lionel Messi.

It has been revealed that cross curated his 25-man list via Mirror Sport by explaining that he's been reporting on football for more than 25 years and, as such, there are many legendary names included along with modern-day stars. Where he ranks the current generation may surprise readers, though it's worth noting he deemed England's 3-2 win over Mexico at the World Cup to be the nation's 'best ever away performance'.

In 25th place is AC Milan hero Marco van Basten, a player who won three Ballons d'Or, though as Cross mentions, he had his career cut short by injuries. The Daily Mirror writer suggests that if not for injuries, he'd have made the top five on this list.

Roberto Carlos is next up, and Cross deemed him a 'brilliant entertainer' and a player who could get you out of your seat, even playing as a left-back. For many fans, this is a fair ranking of the Brazil and Real Madrid icon because there aren't many better players who have played in his position.

The first Premier League name to make Cross's list is Patrick Vieira, with the journalist particularly praising his physicality and leadership. Dubbed 'one of the greatest captains and midfielders to ever grace the English game', the former Arsenal skipper's dominance is hard to deny.

CROSS CONTROVERSY: There was no place for Patrick Vieira's longtime rival Roy Keane in his list.

According to recent reports, paolo Maldini is one of the players you could rank above Carlos on the all-time left-back list, and the Italian icon sits above him on Cross's list. The AC Milan great's peak came during the journalist's childhood, and he recalled watching him during the 1980s and Channel 4's coverage of Serie A.

Another Premier League star, Kevin De Bruyne, earned his place among Cross's favourites. The former Manchester City midfielder was named 'the best player in the best team in English football', though Cross noted that it comes 'with a caveat now' due to the club being found guilty of breaching financial rules.

John Cross' 25 Best Players (25 -21).

Sticking with playmaking gems, Cross ranked Luka Modric 20th, branding him 'the epitome of a European midfielder' and 'the greatest Croatian player in history'. He did, however, point out the Real Madrid legend's lack of understanding that 'football's coming home' is a 'self-deprecating joke at ourselves'.

Industry observers note that in 19th place is David Beckham, maybe the first name that will stir up controversy, whether that be because he's too high or too low. There aren't many more polarising players in history because some use his celebrity status against him, while others, like Cross, believe he approached the ball like a 'work of art'.

Another Englishman, Frank Lampard, takes 18th, and Cross highlighted his goalscoring consistency along with his mindset to work 'so hard' to turn himself into 'one of the world's best'. He attributed Chelsea's most successful period to the highest-scoring midfielder in top-flight history.

Recent findings suggest that cross insisted that 'we have to have a wayward hero in there' and claimed that Eric Cantona 'absolutely fits that bill'. Citing his entertainment value, he described the former French striker as creating 'magic stardust' that helped Manchester United end their wait for a title and dominate that era of the Premier League.

It's clear who Cross sides with in the Lampard vs Steven Gerrard vs Paul Scholes debate as he chose Gerrard in 16th, omitting Scholes from his entire list. He mentioned that the former Liverpool captain's long-range goals and passion made him one of his favourite players, recalled his 2005 Champions League win and remarked that he 'deserved to win more trophies'.

John Cross' 25 Best Players (20-16).

Now we get to the more contentious picks, and names like Wayne Rooney falling outside of the top 10 might upset one or two fans. Cross recalled Rooney's Euro 2004 campaign, calling him 'unstoppable' and a 'street footballer' whose intelligence on and off the pitch doesn't get enough credit.

Recent findings suggest that for some, Mohamed Salah isn't an entertaining player to watch, especially in comparison with the likes of Eden Hazard when that conversation comes up. For Cross, his dribbling ability and success at Liverpool make him a 'clear choice' for his list, deeming him a 'fabulous Premier League legend'.

There's a reason Cross asked Arsenal fans for their thoughts, as many regard Thierry Henry as the greatest Premier League player of all time. Given that this is the main competition he covers, it's somewhat surprising the Frenchman doesn't make the top 10, although he does applaud his mentality and natural ability, calling him one of the best he's seen on a weekly basis.

Cross views Dennis Bergkamp as the greatest Arsenal player he's seen, which is why the Dutchman sits above Henry. His admiration of Bergkamp is made clear when he acknowledges him as 'a game-changer for English football' and cites his finish against Newcastle United as being 'from another world'.

Recent findings suggest that just missing out on the top 10 is Barcelona icon Xavi, who played in a team Cross deemed to be 'the best team in Europe'. There's less analysis of the Spaniard than any other player on his list, as Cross instead chose to focus on Pep Guardiola's team rather than explain Xavi's ranking.

John Cross' 25 Best Players (15-11).

Kicking off Cross's top 10 is Andres Iniesta, whom he referenced in his verdict on Xavi. Between the duo, he argues that Iniesta edges it because of his passing vision and control. He called the 2010 World Cup winner 'just wonderful' and 'a joy to watch'.

Sources indicate that perhaps a more controversial pick is Zlatan Ibrahimovic in ninth, although Cross justified this selection by alluding to the change in opinion of the Swedish striker among English media and fans. He recalled his performance for Sweden in a win over England when he scored 'one of the greatest goals of all time' and believes he is 'one of football's greatest-ever characters'.

Recent findings suggest that kylian Mbappe is ranked eighth, and for the older generation, that is a perfectly acceptable ranking for a player who has been a revelation but has still yet to win a Ballon d'Or. For the younger generation, it might seem somewhat low because of his dominance during the modern era, winning the World Cup at the age of 19.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, a Ballon d'Or winner who did make Cross's top 10 is Harry Kane, and the journalist thinks we haven't fully appreciated the England captain for many years. Alluding to his goalscoring exploits in recent times at Bayern Munich, he claims that the former Tottenham striker has got even better with age.

Sources indicate that ranking Jude Bellingham sixth is Cross's most daring decision, and he defended this by tipping the Real Madrid star to be the best English player of all time. He references England's World Cup win over Mexico, describing the Birmingham-born midfielder's performance as 'amazing' and calling him 'elegant, driven and just wonderful'.

CROSS CONTROVERSY: Jude Bellingham is the highest ranked English player on the list at the age of 23.

John Cross' 25 Best Players (10-6).

The reaction in the comments section suggests Bellingham's spot is the most controversial call. Placing the 'truly beautiful, iconic and inspirational' Zinedine Zidane above him in fifth isn't as bold, and Cross mentions watching the French midfielder 'own the whole pitch' in a random Serie A game for Juventus, possessing 'the best control of any player' he's seen.

Zidane's former Real Madrid teammate Ronaldo Nazario takes fourth spot, a player whom Cross states 'had everything', including 'skill, power and pace'. He reckons that at his peak, he was 'the best player in the world'.

CROSS CONTROVERSY: There's no place for Ronaldo Nazario's former Brazilian teammate Ronaldinho on this entire list.

Cross admits that Cristiano Ronaldo's recent 'diva carry-ons' (his unceremonious Portugal retirement) have put him off. He still acknowledges his 'eye for the spectacular', arguing that since he left Manchester United for Real Madrid in 2009, he isn't sure English football has possessed a player of his calibre.

Sources indicate that taking the runners-up medal in Cross's list is Diego Maradona, though he interestingly claims that 'it's not going to be popular'. The highly reputed journalist calls the late Argentine icon 'unstoppable' and celebrates his 1986 World Cup exploits, claiming that he won Argentina the tournament.

'The greatest dribbler and showman' Cross has ever seen, Lionel Messi, is the best player he has watched in person, and that's often the case for fans who witness the Argentine hero in action. He even reveals that he used to side with Cristiano Ronaldo in the GOAT debate, but deems Messi's 2022 World Cup heroics to have ended that discussion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Luciano Spalletti explains what changed for Juventus at half-time to crush Venezia 4-0, admitting Randal Kolo Muani ‘does not enjoy’ being a centre-forward, but will keep pushing anyway.

The Bianconeri were jeered off the field by their fans at half-time, so there were few signs that they would emerge 4-0 winners against Davide Nicola’s Venezia.

Kerim Alajbegovic went off injured during the break, and Nick Woltemade made an immediate impact off the bench, opening the scoring after a scuffed Weston McKennie effort.

It opened the floodgates, followed by a Teun Koopmeiners strike, Juan Cabal header, and Randal Kolo Muani penalty which the ex-PSG striker had also earned.

“They came on for the second half, making choices, taking decisions, with greater fluidity in the passing, trying to have a team idea,” Spalletti told DAZN Italia.

“In the first half, we gave the ball away too cheaply, there was nobody moving from their positions, nobody following the flow of the pass, so it was fundamental the players recognised we were missing something, which we provided in the second half.”.

The victory made it seem a far more confident performance than it was, and the question marks remain over this Juventus side, especially when they don’t have Woltemade and Kolo Muani starting together upfront.

Notably, Woltemade handed over the penalty kick to his teammate, confirming their strong rapport both on and off the field.

It is surely undeniable now that Kolo Muani is much better on the left as a support striker than as a centre-forward.

“I agree Kolo Muani feels more at ease on the left, but I need someone who can be a centre-forward with all these games. When Nico Gonzalez returns, I will have on the right Nico, Conceicao and Zhegrova, on the left I have Alajbegovic, Yildiz and Boga,” added Spalletti.

Sources indicate that “So I must stimulate him, show that he can do that in the centre, but he has to create that space with his attitude, so he can run into those spaces. When he receives the ball with a man behind him, he has shown it is not something he enjoys, but he can get into that position rather than just standing and being ready to receive the ball.”.

Edon Zhegrova indicated the best and worst of his abilities today, both providing assists and giving the ball away to spark counter-attacks.

“Zhegrova is an incredible player, because at times he does things even he cannot explain. He has this geniality and when it looks impossible, he emerges with a moment that is not written in any tactical books.

“Yet, sometimes he wanders around, checks out of the game, and gives the ball away, like the time when Bremer had to come and clean up. Having this attitude within football becomes fundamental, because just a couple of moments aren’t enough, you need to be consistent throughout the game.”.

This was Spalletti’s 600th Serie A career match as a coach, and he chose to joke about the constant speculation over his potential dismissal at Juventus.

“With everything people say, what is your career objective after hitting 600 games? Reaching the 601st is the answer, because anything can happen in football.”.

All the build-up and all the hype and Mauricio Pochettino's start to life as Manchester United boss could not have got off to a much worse start.

The latest United manager was handed one of the toughest starts to life in the United dugout, with the Red Devils taking on old rivals Liverpool at Anfield.

Pochettino may have been suffering from jet lag, having only arrived in Manchester on Wednesday, after guiding the USA to a two-legged win over Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League, but it was his defenders who looked like they were suffering from the same fatigue on the pitch against the Reds.

There were less than eight minutes on the clock when United were reduced to ten men. Matthijs de Ligt, starting his first Premier League game since November 2025, failed to track the run of Alexander Isak from a long ball forward and Leny Yoro, coming slowly across to cover, brought the Swede down and was sent off.

To make matters worse, Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick and three minutes later, the United defence were at sixes and sevens again and Florian Wirtz volleyed home for 2-0.

Industry observers note that speaking on SKy Sports' Super Sunday coverage, Jamie Carragher said: "It's as bad as it gets from two centre-backs. The ball wasn't even a pass, it was a clearance. Absolutely shocking.".

It has been revealed that fellow co-commentator Gary Neville said: "He's [De Ligt] obviously, to be fair, been out for 12 months, so I do have some sympathy for him. But between them, it's unbelievable from a defensive perspective. It is shocking. And while Manchester United have those types of defenders in their team, they have no chance of keeping clean sheets.".

And that start to the substantial match of the weekend led to another Manchester United legend, Rio Ferdinand, delivering his verdict on what he had seen. He only had two words to say: "TV off.".

Pochettino will have better days ahead, but the extent of the job on his hands at Old Trafford, and of what it will take to revolutionise Man Utd, became crystal clear, if he wasn't fully aware of it beforehand with that dreadful defensive start.

GIVEMESPORT understands that Pochettino will be backed in the January transfer window, and he may well add a new centre-back to his list of priorities.

Age is the obvious consideration.

Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier remarked Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.

The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.

Under Nvidia's bylaws, Huang can be removed "with or without cause" by a majority vote of its 11 directors.

The Fresh York Times first reported that the 63-year-old Huang had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to him.

Later Thursday, Reuters news agency alleged an intimate relationship between Huang and a second employee, citing unidentified sources.

Sources indicate that those revelations emerged just three days after Huang admitted a relationship with a Chinese woman, whom United States intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. The woman, Alice Huang — no relation — is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that runs artificial intelligence (AI) data centers across Southeast Asia and is a major client of Nvidia.

The US government is investigating the startup on suspicion that it secretly sent some of its Nvidia chips to China, violating Washington's curbs on high-end semiconductors.

Those advanced Nvidia processors ‌are ​used to train and run the large AI models behind chatbots and other generative AI products.

Megaspeed denies the allegations and on Thursday pledged to cooperate with US investigators. Huang, the alleged spy, has been barred from entering Singapore and Taiwan — a key chipmaking island.

While Nvidia's board backed its CEO after the first scandal emerged, market watchers believe the second caused too much reputational damage to one of the world's top three companies by market value.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Huang doesn't believe in formal succession planning, so with little notice, Nvidia appointed CFO Kress as interim CEO.

Bloomberg reported Wednesday that Nvidia’s board is working with advisers to identify potential permanent successors.

Kress, other senior Nvidia executives and members of Huang's own family have been mooted as replacements. The family members include his daughter Madison, a senior director of product marketing, and his son Spencer, who presently works in the firm's robotics division.

In a recent development, rumors also abound over a longer-term solution. On India's CNBC-TV18, Jeffrey Sonnenfeld from the Yale School of Management floated former Apple CEO Tim Cook and ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt.

US President Donald Trump also backed Cook on social media, writing: "A Legend replaces a Legend.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The scandals have certainly hit Nvidia's market value. Since the first extramarital affair emerged on Sunday, the chipmaker's market capitalization has fallen by well over $600 billion to $4.2 trillion.

It has been revealed that nvidia shares were down more than 9% in premarket trading Thursday, after dropping by 10% earlier this week. Some analysts expect the stock price to struggle in the short term.

Nvidia stock hit all-time highs just a month ago as US technology giants continued to announce billions in spending on AI infrastructure.

Demand for Nvidia's advanced chips is so high, however, that many market analysts expect little impact on near-term sales.

"While Jensen [Huang] is the heart and lungs of the Nvidia story…the organization and its leading-edge GPU technology will go on and [his departure] does not change the entrenched position Nvidia has in the AI Revolution chip arms race," noted Dan Ives, a partner, senior managing director and tech analyst at Yorkville Ives, a US-based merchant bank.

Analysts see the biggest long-term risk in strategy and execution. After all, Huang was the leader who picked which ideas Nvidia should bet heavily on and got the whole company behind them.

His sudden exit is also seen as highly disruptive to the chip designer's strong relationships with AI hyperscalers, Taiwanese chip producer TSMC and foreign governments — especially China.

Huang was Nvidia's main lobbyist on US chip export rules and persuaded US President Donald Trump to ease some curbs on China last year.

Huang is often called a rockstar CEO for his leather jackets instead of suits.

Like Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, he was also seen as a key-person risk as Nvidia’s public image, strategic direction and technical decisions became closely tied to him.

Huang steered the organization for more than three decades and was also respected for his hands-on involvement in product architecture and engineering decisions.

He also insisted on a flat management structure, with around 60 executives reporting directly to him.

Huang has run the organization so tightly around his own technical judgment and product decisions that investors may have little sense of how it would function without him.

At the same time, Nvidia is no longer the startup Huang founded in 1993. The organization has built deep expertise in chip design and software, creating a durable moat that helps protect its huge profits, which topped $120.1 billion last year.

Some analysts argue that its central role in the AI hardware buildout makes it less dependent on Huang’s day-to-day input.

China is rapidly playing catch-up with the US in the global race for AI dominance.

While Chinese AI models have lagged behind the likes of ChatGPT and Claude, recent updates from DeepSeek, Alibaba and Moonshot have closed much of the gap on benchmark tests and often beat US rivals on cost and speed.

Beijing is also investing heavily in domestic chips and data centers to reduce reliance on US hardware.

The US has curbed exports to China of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips.

However, this move has only slowed the pace of China's AI ambitions.

Reuters reported Thursday that Chinese AI firms are now trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centers outside China, amid fears the US could further tighten restrictions on advanced chips.

Also Thursday, Beijing accused the US of using the Nvidia spying claims as a pretext to impose a technological "blockade" on China.

The problem is likely to dominate talks next week between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC gathering in Shenzhen in southern China.

Since the competition was revamped by UEFA in 2024, no side have made it through to the knock-out round having lost their first three games.

With defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo arriving in quick succession, Martin O’Neill’s men looked to be heading for an early exit.

After beating Besiktas last time out, however, they are still in with a shout when matchday five takes them to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday.

Winger Yang, who made his first start since early September in the win over St Mirren on Saturday, feels there’s a growing belief among the players they can yet emulate last season’s feat of reaching the play-off round.

Industry observers note that ‘Can we make history? Of course,’ he said. ‘We believe we can qualify. We are getting better all the time. You could see that against Besiktas.

Yang made his first start since early September in Celtic's victory over St Mirren on Saturday.

Martin O'Neill aims to keep Celtic's Europa League hopes alive by beating Torreense this week.

Torreense made history last season by becoming the first second-tier team to win the Portuguese Cup and qualify for Europe. Despite right now sitting 13th in that division, they have confounded expectations by taking six points from four Europa League games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Today, as of 10:16 GMT, NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft has journeyed one light-day, or 25.9 billion kilometres, from Earth — farther than any human-made object has gone before. At this distance, signals from Earth’s surface travelling at light speed will take a full 24 hours to reach the craft. The trailblazing probe is expected to lose communications with Earth in 2029, when its plutonium power finally dies. But that time might not signal the end of Voyager 1’s contributions — the craft carries a golden record engraved with sights and sounds from Earth, an interspecies message for any aliens who might encounter it as it continues its journey.

A device that stimulates the brain with flickering light and rhythmic clicking sounds has failed to slow memory loss in people with Alzheimer’s disease. The Spectris AD headset is designed to induce brain activity called gamma waves, which have been linked to increased attention and memory. The results of a long-anticipated clinical trial showed that participants who used the device did not show robust improvements in their cognitive function after a year of treatment compared with those assigned to a sham treatment. The results were reported at the Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's Disease meeting on 16 November.

The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has announced that the United States has lost its measles elimination status amid an outbreak that’s caused more than 5,700 infections and 10 deaths this year. The US had eliminated measles in 2000 after an intensive vaccination campaign. But declining vaccination rates in the past few years have left pockets of the population vulnerable to infection. “We’ve taken an enormous step back in public health,” indicates virologist Paul Offit. Measles has also been re-established in Mexico and Bolivia, PAHO announced.

Source: International Vaccine Access Center, Johns Hopkins University.

Industry observers note that consumer tests that promise to reveal the full range of microbes living in your gut are taking off — but their results can vary widely. “This is an industry that’s running wild,” says genomicist Jacques Ravel, who co-authored a study that tested several providers. With regard to testing methods, he says, “there’s no standard”. But it’s hard to set those standards, writes journalist Amber Dance, who sent off her own stool to investigate the field. Part of the problem is that “there is no known ‘ground truth’ for a natural microbial sample”, she says.

The proportion of reviewers at Nature who are early-career researchers. Increasing it would benefit all researchers and science as a whole, argues a Nature editorial. (Nature | 6 min read).

Amid the tedium of investigating potentially fraudulent papers, “there is some light relief, thanks to some hilarious phrases used by authors seeking to avoid detection by plagiarism checkers”, writes research-integrity sleuth Dorothy Bishop. Bishop and Nature’s careers team have compiled a quiz to test your ability to match ‘tortured phrases’ — those that replace common words with synonyms in an attempt to skirt past plagiarism-detection software — with their original text.

In a recent development, from the Bering Strait to Doggerland, much of human history occurred in places that are now underwater, covered by the sea-level rise that occurs after ice ages. Geographer Jerome Dobson has dubbed this drowned land ‘Aquaterra’. It’s the site of many discoveries — such as Blinkerwall in the Baltic Sea, one of Europe’s oldest and largest Stone Age structures — and possibly many more to come. It also offers an interesting thought experiment: if we continue to drive global warming, what might future archaeologists make of our inundated world?

The Atlantic | 29 min read, intermittent paywall.

Reference: Geographical Review paper (from 2014).

California congressman Jared Huffman is among the US delegates at the COP31 climate conference in Turkey. He notes that the success of a climate-friendly party in recent elections will revive the country’s participation in global negotiations. (The Guardian | 6 min read).

Star striker Antonio Raimondo is still out with a sprained ankle, along with Florian Grillitsch, while Gabriele Bracaglia is suspended and here replaced by Cittadini on the left flank.

Ghedjemis, Romano Schmid and Georgia international Kvernadze therefore start together with the Austrian as a False 9.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal and Liverpool are monitoring Jamal Musiala’s increasingly uncertain situation at Bayern Munich after senior figures at the Bundesliga champions admitted his future could eventually come under consideration.

The 23-year-old remains one of Europe’s most gifted attacking midfielders, but a difficult period with injuries has disrupted his progress.

Arsenal and Liverpool have admired him for years, and any genuine availability in 2027 would immediately create one of the biggest transfer battles of the summer.

According to talkSPORT, Arsenal and Liverpool retain long-standing interest in Musiala, while Chelsea and Manchester City are also monitoring developments.

Crucially, Musiala’s contract until 2030 reportedly contains a €175million (£147m) release clause that becomes active in 2027.

Former Bayern chief Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has also publicly questioned whether the club can continue carrying such a significant financial commitment if Musiala is unable to rediscover his previous level following his recent fitness problems.

However, Bayern have not actively placed him on the market, and Musiala remains focused on succeeding in Munich.

Liverpool’s interest is certainly not newly introduced. CaughtOffside previously reported that the Reds had been tracking Musiala closely, while Arsenal have also been repeatedly linked with the Germany international.

For both clubs, Musiala would represent a genuine statement signing.

Arsenal could use him as a creative left-sided attacker or advanced midfielder, giving Mikel Arteta another elite player capable of breaking down deep defences.

According to recent reports, liverpool would have similar reasons for pursuing him. Musiala’s dribbling, ability to operate between the lines and versatility across several attacking positions would fit naturally into an aggressive, fluid system.

The obvious concern is the cost.

In a recent development, even if Bayern become willing to negotiate below the €175m clause, Musiala would command an enormous fee and salary. His recent injury history would also need to be assessed carefully before either club made that level of commitment.

Still, opportunities to sign a player of Musiala’s quality rarely appear.

Arsenal and Liverpool should therefore remain involved, but there is no reason to rush. If Musiala returns to full fitness and proves he can consistently reproduce his best form, a major 2027 move could suddenly become much easier to justify.

In a recent development, so where do Manchester United go from here? It is never a good look when opposition fans start willing a rival club to stick with their manager, but that was the ignominy that had befallen Michael Carrick by the end of an afternoon in which Lisandro Martinez’s latest plastic hardman impression embodied the very worst of United’s self-sabotage.

After seeing their team go 2-0 up when Cole Palmer converted the penalty given away by Martinez’s lunacy, the Chelsea fans taunted Carrick with chants of “You’re getting sacked in the morning” and later “You’re going down with the City”, a nod to the other Manchester club who are crisis torn for very different reasons.

As the final whistle loomed, though, and with United just grateful Estevao had not punished Martinez’s red card more severely, the Chelsea fans had changed their tune. “Michael Carrick, we want you to stay,” came the chant from the Matthew Harding Stand and that cut far deeper.

And to think that the opening 45 minutes had offered United and their fans some hope of a little respite from the storm before ultimately giving way to an ever-darkening gloom.

Carrick, who had been given a stay of execution in midweek, remarked he still expected to be in charge for Roma’s visit to Old Trafford on Tuesday in the Champions League. But it is hard to escape the feeling that another managerial change will be coming at United before too long even if no one can be sure what happens next.

Equally, the prospect of more upheaval in the dugout might elicit little more than a shrug from fans pointing the finger squarely at the ownership and the executives they have appointed. The players were spared this time but Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers remained the target of sustained abuse as did Jason Wilcox, the director of football.

In a recent development, defeat here extended United’s winless run to nine matches, their worst sequence for 38 years. They have taken just four points from the last 21 on offer in the Premier League and seem to be sinking fast. Carrick was asked about the team becoming mired in a relegation battle. This is the territory United are in.

Industry observers note that the strange thing is this could and probably should have been a day when they at least stopped the rot for a few days. But more non-existent defending and brainlessness from Martinez, who was sent off for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face, put paid to that in a second half in which Carrick admitted United “unravelled”.

Chelsea were cut open on at least five occasions in a see-saw first half and Matheus Cunha also had a goal disallowed for a narrow offside. Xabi Alonso’s side had opportunities of their own – you will always get them against this United team – but they were second best and lucky not to be behind. Everyone talks about United being there for the taking, but the truth is Chelsea, coming off the back of a miserable defeat to Spurs and Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool, were here.

In a recent development, the problem is Carrick’s team could not hit a barn door at the moment. They have scored just three goals in their last six league games and that lack of cutting edge was evident in the way Bruno Fernandes, back in the team as captain, and Amad Diallo (dangerous but with no end product) wasted excellent chances. That wastefulness would put pressure on any back line, let alone one with all the fortitude of wet cardboard. Chelsea were spared and exploited it with the help of the second and most corrosive acts of United’s self-mutilation.

We will come to Martinez’s sending off in a moment, but there had already been a cowardly act of a different kind from the Argentine defender before then in the lead-up to Chelsea’s opening goal soon after the restart.

Sources indicate that take nothing away from Morgan Rogers – his 40yd dash from the edge of the centre circle in United’s half to the six-yard box and the finish that followed were top notch. But where was the challenge? How could not a single player in red have stood in his path? “Come on Morgan, run through us buddy” seemed to be the message.

According to recent reports, by the end, with Estevao – making the most of a first league start of the season – running riot and Chelsea smelling blood, Carrick would have been relieved the scoreline was not worse. But he will also have wondered how United could again have found themselves in such a position after an enterprising first half when they attacked with pace and purpose and looked a very different team to the one that had been ransacked by Como and Bournemouth.

Michael Carrick stated he expects to be in charge of Manchester United next week despite Lisandro Martinez’s moment of madness leaving the club mired in a relegation battle and on their worst run for 38 years.

United were urged to sell Martinez after the controversial Argentina defender was sent off for elbowing Wesley Fofana as Carrick accused his side of “unravelling” as they slumped to a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea.

According to recent reports, it left United without a win in nine matches, their worst run since 1988, and at risk of being sucked into the relegation zone. They have won just two of 13 games this season.

Recent findings suggest that the Old Trafford hierarchy gave Carrick a stay of execution in midweek and, when asked if he expected to still to be at the helm when United face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday, the head coach replied: “Yes. I’m just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek now.”.

Industry observers note that having been booked moments earlier for a foul on Morgan Rogers, Martinez was sent off for a second yellow. The incident came less than three weeks after the Argentinian was fined and publicly apologised for attacking United director of football Jason Wilcox and the board over transfer policy and was the latest in a series of mistakes from him on the pitch this season.

Joe Cole, the former Chelsea and England forward, believes United must get rid of Martinez.

It has been revealed that “Whatever the next Manchester United looks like, Lisandro Martinez has run his course,’ Cole said on TNT Sports. “He’s at the scene of the crime too often for Manchester United and is at fault for moments and goals like that. So that’s probably his time done.”.

Carrick refused to publicly criticise Martinez but admitted his dismissal was a “huge moment” and felt his team “unravelled” in the second period.

“Things have gone against us in a major way,” the United manager noted. “It’s unravelled promptly. There’s a lot of emotion right now. It’s a huge moment in the game. Sometimes you get setbacks in games and you’ve got to deal with that better. I’ve not seen it [the Martinez incident] back so I don’t know if it was [a red card] or not. He’s gone to it and the referee gave that decision, but it’s a big moment.”.

Asked if there would be a stigma attached to United potentially dropping into the relegation zone, Carrick added: “Not for me, no.”.

Industry observers note that and when asked how his players would deal with a relegation battle, Carrick added: “We’ve got to keep moving forward and winning games. There’s no words I’m going to explain to you now that makes any difference, it’s not going to change it. We’ve got to move forward and win matches.”.

What do football fans actually want from their club owners? The model for most has been Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan and friends at Manchester City, owners whose hands are put frequently into pockets of unlimited depth, have made vast improvements to every aspect of the club and its community and are rarely ever seen, let alone heard from.

That view may have to evolve after certain verdicts about certain charges, but few envious glances from around the country have been cast towards the owners of Manchester’s other major club.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The men, both in their 40s, were arrested last year, with Iran repeatedly rejecting the allegations against them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two Iranian men were found guilty of spying on dissident journalists in Britain on behalf of Iran's Revolutionary Guard on Thursday.

British counterterrorism police remarked the case reflected intensifying hostile Iranian activity in the country, an matter that recently made headlines amid the security scare at the RAF Fairford airbase that's a major operational site in Europe for the US Air Force.

The men, both in their 40s, were arrested last year, with Iran repeatedly rejecting the allegations against them.

The Woolwich Crown Court in London convicted one of the Iranian citizens not just of spying on journalists working for the Persian-language dissident TV channel Iran International, but of plotting a violent attack against one or more of them.

The second individual had also faced charges of plotting an attack but was only convicted of spying on the reporters.

One of the convicted defendants said he was acting under duress after his family was threatened, and the other said he did not know that his actions were assisting Iranian intelligence.

A third defendant, a 57-year-old Iranian man, was acquitted of all charges.

The men were accused of engaging in conduct likely to assist the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Iran's multi-discipline military force that's seen as closer to the country's religious leadership and more influential than its regular armed forces.

The UK formally designated the IRGC as a threat to national security in July, meaning that supporting or assisting the organization can carry penalties of up to 14 years in prison as part of new rules on national security and state threats.

Sentencing in this case is still pending and is scheduled for mid-December.

"This was a calculated operation to spy on those critical of the Iranian regime," stated Frank Ferguson, chief prosecutor for the Crown Prosecution Service's special crime and counter-terrorism division.

The two men were accused of visiting addresses linked to their targets, taking photos and videos, and using platforms such as ChatGPT to research them online.

"Thankfully, the defendants were stopped before any attack could take place," prosecutor Ferguson said.

Senior ‌National Coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing Vicki Evans noted that the IRGC or "middlemen" for Iranian intelligence were directing the plot.

Iran's government had repeatedly denied the allegations, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying he was "disturbed" by the trio's arrests last May.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

There have been four cases targeting the Persian language television channel Iran International since late 2023.

In July, two Romanian men were jailed for stabbing a journalist outside his home in 2024.

A spokesman for the broadcaster's parent organization, Volant Media, said in a statement that Thursday's verdicts "don't make the lives of our journalists any safer so long as the Islamic Republic of Iran continues its campaign of death threats and violence against them.".

Iran International reported that a British barrister was also one of the targets.

British law enforcement has been warning of an uptick of hostile Iranian activity in recent years, particularly since the US military operations against Tehran began earlier this year.

Most notably, the UK has accused Iran of being behind a suspected plot targeting the RAF Fairford base in September, after which US President Donald Trump withdrew some long-range bombers from the site.

Three men were indicted in the US in relation to that plot this week, while two others currently face charges in the UK.

According to recent reports, but beyond this, the head of Britain's MI5 domestic intelligence agency Ken MacCullum mentioned in October that Iran-linked operations had led to more than 50 arrests in the last year. He also said known cases of so-called state threats had more than quadrupled in a decade.

Counter-terrorism police chief Evans said she expected this trend to continue.

France this week also accused Iran of being behind a cyberattack targeting refrigeration units at hundreds of supermarkets in October, although Iran denied any involvement.

According to recent reports, european governments are on heightened alert for so-called hybrid warfare tactics, from Russia as well as Iran, amid the geopolitical tensions of recent years. Newly introduced technologies like low-cost drones and AI are also threatening to make such activities cheaper, harder to trace, and potentially more effective.
