📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is reportedly safe for now as there is the acceptance that he needs to be shown patience and given time at Stamford Bridge.

The Spanish tactician only took over Chelsea in the summer, having previously been very highly regarded during his time as Bayer Leverkusen manager.

Still, there’s no escaping the fact that Chelsea have made a poor start to this campaign, with more details available for you to read here just to put things into perspective.

According to the Daily Mail, however, Alonso is safe as Chelsea manager for now, so the 44-year-old should get the chance to try to turn things around.

Alonso was never likely to hit the ground running in what has proven to be a really challenging job for a number of managers in recent times, but there’s clearly still room for improvement.

The Mail’s report points out, however, that Leverkusen were initially inconsistent under Alonso’s management, having a very stop-start first season before an incredible unbeaten title-winning campaign in his second.

Even if Alonso doesn’t look entirely convincing in some ways, CFC need to look at other clubs that have been a bit more patient and willing to back their managers.

The best example of this is Mikel Arteta at Arsenal, but of course it’s also true of Alonso at Leverkusen, and previously with Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool.

And a lot of people forget this, but even Pep Guardiola’s first season at Manchester City was pretty bad as they finished third and failed to win any silverware.

Hungary on Thursday said it would ease abortion rules and ratify an international treaty on violence against women.

Under the planned changes to the so-called "heartbeat regulation," women will no longer be forced to listen to the vital signs of the fetus before an abortion.

Women will also be able to get emergency contraceptive pills without prescription.

The changes proposed by the new government under Prime Minister Peter Magyar are a significant break with the conservative policies of his predecessor Viktor Orban.

The country also plans to ratify the Istanbul Convention, a treaty aimed at preventing violence against women and domestic violence.

Hungarian law allows for most abortions to be performed up to 12 weeks, and up to 24 weeks in cases of severe developmental abnormalities. Until now, women were required to have a medical provider show them evidence of a definitive sign of fetal life, commonly understood as the so-called "fetal heartbeat," before deciding whether to have an abortion.

The controversial 2022 policy had received widespread criticism from doctors and women’s rights groups as being cruel and humiliating. It will now be scrapped.

The policy had not led to a decline in abortions and according to Magyar, had raised "serious bioethical questions.".

The second major change is that emergency contraception will be available without prescription.

Further measures include changing the criminal code aimed at better protecting women, including making the misuse of intimate images a criminal offense and strengthening the treatment of victims of domestic violence during criminal proceedings.

Hungary also looks to ratify an international treaty on the protection of women which most other EU members have long ratified. The Istanbul Convention came into force in 2014 and, among other things, requires rape to be criminalized based on the absence of freely given consent.

"We are making it clear that sexual acts can only ⁠take ​place with the voluntary consent of the other party," ​Magyar stated.

The government of his predecessor Orban had opposed the treaty, arguing that it promoted what it described as "gender ideology.".

"We are making a clear and accountable commitment to putting an end to the era of inaction," Magyar mentioned in a Facebook video.

Among the EU’s other members, only Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Lithuania and Slovakia have not yet ratified the convention.

The Istanbul Convention is a treaty by the Council of Europe, an international organization that promotes human rights and the rule of law across Europe and includes more countries than the member of the EU.

Recent findings suggest that this Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

Sources indicate that looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. Maxim de Cuyper, a £17.5m arrival from Club Brugge, was credited with the assist after Yasin Ayari tapped in.

Ayari cost £3.5m from Swedish club AIK and scored in the 5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace, and now has this winner to add to his collection. The 23-year-old is another example of Brighton polishing these gems and putting them together in a team that can win against any opponent in the Premier League.

It could keep them at the top end of the table for a good while longer. They have already shown they can defeat Arsenal in a one-off match and they look to have the ingredients to stay the pace with them. In Fabian Hürzeler they have one of the brightest young coaches in the Premier League and he has a squad that are all on the same page.

Leicester upset the odds 10 years ago with a settled team, while this Brighton team has a deeper squad. When the substitutes came on in the second half, they slotted into a well-rehearsed system.

“We faced adversity. There was a little bit of luck but in the end they deserved it because they worked hard for it,” remarked Hürzeler. “I want players who want to compete, to dominate. They all have the winning mentality inside of them. These kinds of performances are not about one or two players, everyone has to stick together.”.

Hürzeler has played down a title challenge but his team have been among the most impressive in the first part of the season. Next is Getafe in the Europa Conference League on Thursday.

While Hürzeler was reluctant to name individual performers, Dutch goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen was another key player in this win. He kept out Iliman Ndiaye and repelled Erling Haaland, who lost a physical battle with Lewis Dunk. “You’re going down with the Palace,” chanted the jubilant Brighton fans, with City now losing two Premier League games in a row.

City head coach Enzo Maresca will be content with the number of chances his team created but there must be concerns at the other end. He tried a change of formula, dropping Marc Guéhi to the bench for the first time this season, yet his team were still prone to individual errors.

“We are the second team in scoring in the Premier League. We are scoring goals but in this moment we are conceding silly goals. We can avoid that,” Maresca said. His team have conceded 10 goals in their last six games, which is not the foundation of a title challenge, even if City have been stacking up points.

Maresca picked a midfield that cost £327m to recruit this summer, with Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi picked together for the first time. Pascal Gross cost a nominal fee when he returned to Brighton but his hard work and intelligent passing means Brighton can control periods of the game even against the very best.

Sources indicate that the goal came when Brighton switched play from a free-kick, although City thought Anderson was victim rather than perpetrator. Former Inter Miami winger Gómez provided the cross that opened up City, with Gianluigi Donnarumma guilty of not coming out to claim the ball, then Matheus Nunes slipped at the vital moment.

According to recent reports, “Unfortunately it is happening for our players but I think it is part of the game, part of football, it happens many times against us, we need to analyse and understand what we can do better,” Maresca added. City also felt Dunk used his arm to block the ball in the penalty area, although no spot-kick was given.

In a recent development, it was a sweet goal by Ayari, who had missed a penalty in the shoot-out last week when the teams played in the EFL Cup. Brighton stayed in Manchester after the defeat, masterminding a win that means they have now defeated all of the traditional heavyweight teams in the Premier League.

It has been revealed that “I wasn’t aware of that. For me it’s more key, not about history, it’s about giving something back to the supporters. They’ve spent a lot of time and money,” Hürzeler remarked.

“We’ll take it game by game. See what happens because we have loads of games. Just focussing every day on what’s ahead of us and the job we have. We will continue to do that and see where it leaves us at the end of the season. We are happy with the way we are playing - not just the results but the way we are playing too. We have to continue to develop that style and ruthlessness and we can do great things.”.

Kings of the jungle? This early human had surprising survival skills that rivalled ours

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S.
  • Sources indicate that homo erectus is already one of humans’ most extraordinary ancient relatives.
  • Did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S. Entressangle/E. Daynes/SPL.

Sources indicate that homo erectus is already one of humans’ most extraordinary ancient relatives. The massive-brained, tool-wielding species emerged two million years ago in Africa and expanded across Eurasia, before vanishing around 100,000 years ago in Java, Indonesia.

Did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate? Tooth proteins hint at ancient trysts.

It has been revealed that did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate? Tooth proteins hint at ancient trysts.

Researchers have now added another feather to the hominin’s cap. A pair of studies analysing fossil teeth1,2, which were published in Nature on 18 November, suggest that H. erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago.

In a recent development, researchers had thought that H. erectus was limited to savannahs and open woodlands, notes Kira Westaway, a geochronologist at Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia, and a co-author of both studies.

According to recent reports, “Never, ever have we seen them in rainforests,” she adds. “This is a really major deal, because we thought Homo sapiens were the only species that had the skill set to survive in really challenging rainforest environments.”.

Sources indicate that the earliest H. erectus fossils, from eastern Africa, are 1.9 million years old. But the svelte, upright-walking and running hominins wasted little time, reaching western Asia and present-day China some 200,000 years later and modern Java, using land bridges, not long after. The last-known H. erectus remains, from central Java, date to roughly 110,000 years ago3.

Limestone caves in Guangxi province, southern China, contained more than 10,000 fossil teeth.Credit: Kira Westaway (Macquarie University).

While looking for fossils from a three-metre-tall great ape called Gigantopithecus, Westaway and her colleagues identified a pair of limestone caves in Guangxi province in southern China. There, they discovered more than 10,000 fossil teeth from animals such as orangutans (Pongo spp.), monkeys and wild boar (Sus spp.), as well as 9 from hominins. The researchers estimate that the hominins lived between 184,000 and 324,000 years ago, according to dating of both fossils and the surrounding sediments using various methods.

Recent findings suggest that eight of the hominin teeth resembled those of H. erectus in their shape, a designation that was confirmed by analysing the sequences of proteins preserved in the dental enamel of four specimens, states co-author Frido Welker, a molecular palaeoanthropologist at the University of Copenhagen.

The tooth enamel was analysed and its proteins sequenced.Credit: Kira Westaway (Macquarie University).

Recent findings suggest that the ninth lacked the shape and protein signature of H. erectus teeth, says Welker, and it also didn’t resemble those of H. sapiens or Neanderthals (Homo neanderthalensis). Denisovans — enigmatic ancient humans first discovered in southern Siberia and now linked to diverse fossils from China and elsewhere in Asia — are a possibility, but the evidence is circumstantial, says Welker. “Every label we put on that ninth tooth is a little bit of speculation.”.

Sources indicate that the multitude of animal teeth was probably accumulated by a scavenger such as a porcupine. The presence of fossils from species such as muntjac deer (Muntiacus muntjac), leopards and orangutans hints at a rainforest environment.

Roberto D’Aversa saw his debut on the Sassuolo bench ruined by a Milutin Osmajic double, as Genoa emerged with all three points from this relegation battle, inflicting a sixth straight defeat.

The Neroverdi sacked coach Alberto Aquilani following a run of one point from seven rounds, including five defeats on the bounce going into the break for international duty.

D’Aversa could not count on injured Cristian Volpato, Daniel Boloca, Ismael Koné and Fedde Leysen, with Domenico Berardi and Vasilije Adzic carrying knocks too. Genoa saw their three-match winning streak ended by a 2-1 defeat to Milan, but Morten Frendrup was their only absentee.

See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog.

Armand Laurienté and Fali Candé had predictable long-range attempts early on, as did Berardi at the end of a counter-attack, but it was Genoa who broke the deadlock with their first real attempt.

A long Justin Bijlow goal kick was knocked down by Tommaso Baldanzi, then Hamed Traoré against his old club picked the through ball for Milutin Osmajic, who flicked it in off the outside of the right boot from seven yards.

Genoa added another when Candé gave it away cheaply with an error, allowing Junior Messias to set up Osmajic, who needed a couple of attempts to get past Arijanet Muric in goal.

Sassuolo continued to be ineffective in the final third, as when Laurienté robbed Alex Amorim to set up Berardi, the captain couldn’t keep his finish down.

The first genuine save made by Bijlow was to palm the Laurienté screamer out from under the bar, yet Osmajic and Leo Ostigard had efforts charged down in a mad scramble after a free kick.

Ignace van der Brempt also made a crucial interception to stop Osmajic meeting the Franz-Ethan Meichtry roll across from six yards, while Laurienté curled wide of the far post.

Industry observers note that johan Vasquez made a crucial clearance on the Laurienté free kick, but Genoa lost striker Lorenzo Colombo just a few minutes after his introduction, as he badly sprained his knee. The substitutions had been completed, so they were down to 10 men from the 88th minute, but Berardi only managed to sting Muric’s gloves at the near post.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Celtic returned to action after the international break with a thumping 4-1 win against St Mirren at Celtic Park.

According to recent reports, goals from Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Camilo Duran and Luke McCowan put Celtic in a commanding three-nil lead going into half-time. Callum McGregor made it four for Martin O'Neill's side, and although Killan Phillips pulled one back for the visitors, the Hoops saw out the remainder of the game to maintain their four-point gap at the top of the Scottish Premiership table.

It has been revealed that it was a comfortable result in the end for Celtic, who were missing Alistair Johnston and Mika Baur through injuries. Oxlade-Chamberlain and McCowan were both drafted into the starting XI and impressed, giving O'Neill some selection headaches.

In a recent development, while Oxlade-Chamberlain proved he can still cut it at the top level, Joel van den Berg's cameo off the bench may give O'Neill something to think about. Indeed, the 19-year-old Dutchman caught the eye after coming on in the 61st minute.

Van den Berg joined Celtic from PSV for £3million in the summer and has had to wait for his debut after recovering from an ankle problem. The 2007-born midfielder had featured for the club's B team against Ross County before playing in a bounce game on Tuesday, only to sustain a knock which stopped him from training with the rest of his teammates on Thursday.

In a recent development, but Van den Berg declared himself fit for Friday's session and was then named in the matchday squad to face St Mirren. With Celtic 3-0 up and cruising, O'Neill decided to give him a chance to impress for the final half an hour.

It has been revealed that it's safe to suggest Van den Berg took it with both hands and revealed why he should be getting more minutes with an all-action cameo. A tall, significant and physical midfielder, the Netherlands international made an impression on his first appearance for the Hoops, making 15 successful passes (out of 17), completing one accurate cross and having 32 touches of the ball.

From a defensive point-of-view, Van den Berg looked even better. He won FOUR tackles, made one interception, two clearances and won seven ground duels. Having played just 29 minutes plus stoppage-time, that is a very impressive statistical total.

He received rave reviews from the Celtic fans on social media, who were pleased with his physical output and how he managed to settle into the game, despite St Mirren pushing for a comeback.

With Baur expected to be out for TEN weeks with an ankle injury, Van den Berg should be given more game time and handed a chance to show why Celtic paid £3m for him in the summer. He should be rotated alongside Oxlade-Chamberlain in the middle of the park for now, before then becoming a more regular member in the XI, especially given the talent he has at his disposal.

Sources indicate that celtic are no doubt going to miss Baur and his influence on the team, but Van den Berg can soften the blow if he produces the same level of performance as he did in the cameo against St Mirren. Heading into Thursday's Europa League trip to Torreense, Van den Berg should start along with McGregor in the middle, offering Oxlade-Chamberlain a rest.

After the win against St Mirren, O'Neill praised Van den Berg for his impact as a second-half substitute. “I thought he did really well," the Irishman said. "He’s coming on. He, again, had an injury that kept him out some time. A wee bit frustrating for him in that sense.

“He played up in the B team game at Ross County. He found that tough going. I think the whole team did that night against a very strong Ross County team. But he came back, played in the bounce game on Tuesday. Didn’t do too badly. Came off with an ankle injury. Didn’t train on Thursday. We were concerned, thought he might not make it, but made himself available to train on Friday, which is great. And got into the squad. I thought he did really fine. Really, really well.”.

Needless to say, this is not the start Mauricio Pochettino wanted as Man Utd manager, but this is the reality of the team he’s inherited.

Things are really bad for the Red Devils, so bad in fact that they’ve now gone one further than their awful start in the 1986/87 season when they failed to keep a clean sheet in their opening ten games.

United matched that unwanted stat in their last game and they’re now extending that run, while they’re not too far away from breaking another record.

In the Premier League era, United’s longest run without a clean sheet is 14 games in the 2019/20 season, and you wouldn’t bet against this side matching or breaking that record soon.

United take on Brentford in their next game, and then Newcastle away, so on current form you’d probably expect this struggling MUFC defence to concede in those matches.

Still with Pochettino now at the helm they’ll be hoping to show some improvement soon, with the Argentine known for making his Tottenham teams really defensively solid during his time there.

This was always going to be a huge challenge, however, and there surely needs to be some major work done in the transfer market as well as the change in manager to help get this club back on track.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 14:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 14:09 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • A drone spied on his first training session, his star striker stayed up into the early hours obsessing over Grand Theft Auto the day he arrived, his best player has paused contract talks, his chief executive praised the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and the club banned four supporters for three years for throwing a tennis ball on to the pitch.
  • That was before the football started.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 14:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 14:09 EST, 22 November 2026.

A drone spied on his first training session, his star striker stayed up into the early hours obsessing over Grand Theft Auto the day he arrived, his best player has paused contract talks, his chief executive praised the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and the club banned four supporters for three years for throwing a tennis ball on to the pitch.

That was before the football started. And the fates had decreed that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge as head coach of this slow motion car crash of a football club that was once Manchester United but which has lost all sense of its place in the modern football firmament was to be away to Liverpool at Anfield.

Sources indicate that and Pochettino picked a centre-half, Matthijs de Ligt, who had not started a Premier League game for more than a year. And De Ligt began the game by watching a long ball sail over his head as if it were a rare curiosity to be observed rather than to be dealt with and before you could blink, Leny Yoro had been sent off trying to clear up De Ligt’s mess.

So at least Pochettino got to see United set a newly introduced record. Yoro was sent off after seven minutes and 23 seconds and that has never been done before in the league. So there was that. De Ligt went on, it is sad to report, to have such a dreadful game that it was tempting to look away. Not the best selection decision by the new boss.

And in the stands, Omar Berrada, the strangely bullish United chief executive, looked colder and colder in the chill and, beside him, Jason Wilcox, the director of football, slid deeper and deeper into his warm coat until he nearly disappeared from view. Which, presumably, was what he was hoping to do.

And in the row behind them, Sir Alex Ferguson gazed down on what remained of the great club he had built. James Nesbitt, the wonderful actor who is Ferguson’s friend, sat next to him in the directors’ box. One of Nesbitt’s best performances was in The Missing. The United defence were starring in the remake.

Mauricio Pochettino was given a near-impossible task in his first game as manager of Manchester United.

Leny Yoro (right) was sent off just minutes into their 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool at Anfield.

The Reds dominated from then on, with teenage winger Rio Ngumoha one of the Reds' stars.

Recent findings suggest that and the Liverpool fans loved it. ‘You’re going down with the City,’ they sang at the United fans. ‘You’re getting sacked in the morning,’ they sang at Pochettino, as he stood, arms tightly folded on the touchline. When it got to 4-0, the Kop broke out another ditty. ‘Poch is at the wheel,’ they sang over and over again.

So, welcome to Manchester, Mauricio. Welcome to the sight of United consolidating their position one off the bottom of the Premier League. If they keep this going for another week, they will be in the bottom three of the top flight in December for the first time in more than 50 years. If Pochettino did not know it before, he knows it now: there is an awful lot of saving to be done on the red side of Manchester.

Sources indicate that if Pochettino thought getting the USA to win the World Cup was a major ask, rebuilding United is up there. This is a club mired in dysfunction on and off the pitch. It is a Herculean task to rescue them and we are about to find out whether Pochettino has it in him.

In a recent development, in Jack Kerouac’s novel On the Road, his characters are poised between the East of their past and the West of their future. Pochettino is there, too, caught between the promise of the Southampton and Spurs years and the stasis of PSG, Chelsea and the USA. What happens at United will determine his legacy.

Sources indicate that it was strange seeing a latest United manager anointed at Anfield as the crowd sang You’ll Never Walk Alone and the Kop flew its flags and the faces of Shankly, Paisley, Dalglish, Klopp and the rest stared down from the banner of all the bosses here who have won league titles. Pochettino stood on the sideline and drank it all in, right until kick off.

It was his misfortune that this is also a Liverpool team beginning to click. Florian Wirtz is beginning to express himself and that is a wonderful sight. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak are becoming a formidable partnership. Rio Ngumoha scared Diogo Dalot rigid. Liverpool are rising again as United flounder.

United have not won a Premier League match since Sunday, August 30 when they beat Ipswich 5-2. It is their only victory in the league. For all their problems over the last decade or more, it still felt surreal to look at the table before kick-off and see them sitting below that dotted line, second from bottom.

It did not take long for Pochettino to get his first look at the uselessness that has afflicted United for most of this season. Only seven minutes had gone when Ronald Araujo drove a searching ball over the top of the United defence. De Ligt watched it go and abrogated responsibility for it, expecting Yoro to cover. Isak sprinted after it and by the time Yoro finally reacted, it was too late. Isak was on to it.

Pochettino opted to start Matthijs de Ligt (right) - but he struggled throughout the game.

He knows the size of the task of saving United - and whether he can do it will determine his legacy as a manager.

Liverpool, meanwhile, are starting to click - and Florian Wirtz is at the centre of that rise.

Isak got ahead of Yoro and pushed the ball forwards. It was a heavy touch and would have run on to Lammens but Yoro compounded his error by bundling Isak down on the edge of the area. He was sent off by referee Sam Barrott. Only seven minutes and 23secs had elapsed. It was the quickest sending off in United’s Premier League history. It was not a controversy. It was just a show of defensive incompetence.

Industry observers note that A free-kick in that kind of position might as well be a penalty when Dominik Szoboszlai is standing over it. He lashed it low and hard past the edge of the United wall. Bruno Fernandes shook a half-interested leg at it. It whistled past him and bulged the corner of the United net.

Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araujo (Gomez 85), Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez; Szoboszlai, Mac Allister (Nyoni 72); Barcola (Munoz 72), Wirtz, Ngumoha (Frimpong 78); Isak (Koumas 85).

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Tsimikas, McConnell, Chiesa.

Goals: Szoboszlai 10, Wirtz 13, Ngumoha 66, Munoz 82.

Man United (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, De Ligt, Martinez; Tielemans (Mount 65), Mainoo (Santos 87); Mbeumo (Maguire 22), Fernandes, Dorgu (Mazraoui 65); Cunha (Zirkzee 46).

Subs not used: Heaton, Heaven, Diallo, Lacey.

Industry observers note that three minutes later, Liverpool were further ahead. Rio Ngumoha embarrassed Diogo Dalot down the Liverpool left – not for the last time – and pulled a cross back for Florian Wirtz. It was just behind the Germany playmaker but Wirtz has beautiful technique and somehow, he hooked it goalwards with his left foot and it crashed in off the underside of the bar.

According to recent reports, united were in chaos. Pochettino looked stunned. He brought on Harry Maguire for Mbeumo after 22 minutes. Maybe it was a bitter pill for Mbeumo. Maybe it will have just allowed him to spend more time on his PlayStation. Practice makes perfect, after all.

According to recent reports, and so United spent the rest of the half repelling a siege of their goal. Fernandes summoned one shot on target but it dribbled apologetically through to Alisson from the edge of the area. Most of the time, though, it was like the Alamo at the United end. Maguire made one particularly heroic block from Isak.

Liverpool should have gone three-nil up just before the hour. Wirtz played a fine through ball to Barcola, who ran clear of the defence. Barcola had only Lammens to beat but instead of slotting the ball past him, he tried to dribble around him, got his feet mixed up and kicked the ball out of play.

Sources indicate that there was frustration at Anfield. They wanted more than this. This was a chance to rub United’s noses in it, to inflict more misery on their hapless rivals. And yet, there was a sense they were letting them off the hook.

In a recent development, that feeling deepened when De Ligt made a dreadful mess of intercepting a lofted pass to Isak, missed his kick and fell over. Isak raced through but then blasted his shot hopelessly high and wide. Then Barcola turned De Ligt and hit another shot too high.

Industry observers note that liverpool could not keep missing all afternoon, though, and they finally got their third when Barcola skipped past Lisandro Martinez on the halfway line as if he wasn’t there and sprinted down the right. He squared the ball across the box to Ngumoha and Ngumoha slammed it unerringly past Lammens. Victor Munoz drilled home the fourth eight minutes from time and United’s humiliation was complete.

The point takes Newcastle up to 12th in the Premier League table, meaning they've lost just once in their last four matches.

Newcastle then found themselves in the lead after 62 minutes, as Malick Thiaw pounced in the box to poke home from a set piece.

Arsenal did find an equaliser later in the half through Noni Madueke, but it was certainly a good point overall for Newcastle.

Jaissle deserves plenty of credit for helping Newcastle turn the game around. Being 1-0 down against Arsenal at half-time is far from a disaster, but that didn't stop the Newcastle manager from making a ruthless decision at the break.

Industry observers note that jaissle opted to take Amar Dedic, Jacob Murphy, and Sean Steur off at half-time. On came Tino Livramento, Anthony Elanga, and Jacob Ramsey, with Newcastle finding an equaliser less than five minutes later.

It was a ruthless decision from Jaissle, particularly due to the fact that it was only 1-0 against the side who were sitting top of the Premier League table.

The Newcastle manager knew it wasn't good enough and wanted to do something about it immediately, so he deserves plenty of credit for that.

Although the trio didn't directly influence the game, the brutal nature of the decision from Jaissle clearly gave the players the motivation they needed.

According to recent reports, jaissle clearly isn't here to make friends. Many have been calling for more regular starts for Steur, but the Newcastle boss wasn't happy with his performance and dragged him off.

As mentioned, being 1-0 down to Arsenal is far from a disaster, but it shows the mentality of Jaissle that he wasn't satisfied and wanted to see a lot more from his team.

Nobody seems to be talking about the triple change from Jaissle, perhaps due to the fact that none of the three players got themselves on the scoresheet or created a goal.

It can't be understated how crucial it was for Newcastle to react in the second half, and Jaissle's decision played a huge role in helping that.

In a recent development, ruben Amorim admits Serie A is educational for him, as he is stunned by Frosinone’s tactical tweaks against Milan today. ‘There’s a lot of knowledge in this league, we need to be ready for anything.’.

It kicks off at San Siro at 17.00 GMT (18.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s five Serie A games on the Liveblog.

The biggest problem for the Rossoneri this season has been consistency, as they seem to follow one strong performance with a disastrous result in the next, which has left them struggling in the Europa League more than Serie A.

Frosinone are without Antonio Raimondo, Florian Grillitsch and suspended Gabriele Bracaglia, but surprisingly opt for a False 9 system rather than starting Daniel Birligea upfront.

“It’s strange to see that, we tried to look right away for one time they played like this,” Amorim told DAZN Italia and Sky Sport Italia.

“The managers are really smart and know how to adapt to the opponent, there’s a lot of knowledge in this league. It’s fun, but on the other side we need to be ready for anything.”.

Mike Maignan shook off a knock on international duty to start in goal, but Strahinja Pavlovic is still not at 100 per cent, with Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek and Alexis Saelemaekers still injured.

It is a front three of Goncalo Ramos, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic, who were all in action for their countries last week, but are they suited together when Ramos works harder for the team than the team works for him?

“The most crucial thing if you see Roma, the principles and rotation of the team is more clear than for us. We need time to achieve that, and we had injuries that changed our way of playing, so we need time to work on every principle,” replied Amorim.

“The characteristics of the players are key, but Rabiot is a player who can give goals, Pulisic and Moreira can give goals, so it’s more the principles of the team and the rotation of the team than the characteristics of the players.

“Let’s see during the game, of course you can see the data and the runs behind are what we need to do more. We need to be more clear in the positions, so let’s see today.”.

The transfer window is coming up in January, and RedBird patron Gerry Cardinale has made no secret of the fact he is pursuing Real Madrid talent Endrick.

Cardinale is having a very hands-on approach now, and is on the touchline during the warm-up chatting to former Milan player Simon Kjaer.

Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row.
  • This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be.
  • It has been revealed that roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row. Three different managers have been sacked in that time, and the mood in north London had plunged to grim lows, but finally there is a sense that something truly exciting is stirring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be. After Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, Spurs simply had to make their numerical advantage count. They did so with relative ease, taking complete control of possession and creating endless goalscoring opportunities.

It has been revealed that roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149. The goals ultimately came from two defenders, Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke, but there was a long list of Spurs players who might have scored here.

Spurs take the lead through an Archie Gray header! ⚪ https://t.co/qSCECkOJur.

According to recent reports, did this defeat mark the end for Pierre Sage, the Palace manager? The Frenchman was only appointed in June but it has been a grisly start to the campaign. Palace have the worst defence in the league, have lost six of nine games and have not produced any truly encouraging performances in the Premier League.

Even in the two games Palace have won, against Fulham and Nottingham Forest, they were lucky to do so. The likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank, both of whom would be strong candidates to replace Sage if Palace do pull the trigger, will no doubt have been keeping an eye on events here.

Recent findings suggest that “I am really aware of the situation,” Sage stated. “I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [his future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have 10 years, I will give my best for 10 years.”.

The decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish, then, is whether this result represented a continuation of the team’s problems or was an aberration caused by the early red card. It would be reasonable for Sage to claim this match was out of his hands from the moment Mateta lunged at Spurs captain Micky van de Ven, but such an argument might not carry much weight with Palace sitting 18th in the table.

The challenge was foolish in the extreme by Mateta, a player who was much more successful in exiting this game than he has been in his numerous attempts to leave Palace in recent transfer windows. At first glance it did not seem the worst tackle, but the replays were damning: Mateta led with his studs and made forceful contact with Van de Ven’s ankle.

In a recent development, it was an inexcusably brainless act, after just 13 minutes of play, and the same could be stated of Palace’s defending from a right-wing corner a few minutes later. Mohammed Kudus swirled the delivery to the back post, where Gray was unmarked. Yes, Palace were defending with 10. But no, that does not justify the inability of Sage’s players to spot Gray. Even more embarrassingly, the Tottenham player was unmarked again from another corner shortly afterwards.

It was not the first time this season that Palace’s cause has been undermined by a red card. When they lost at home to Ipswich Town in September, Axel Disasi was sent off after 34 minutes. An absence of discipline? Perhaps. Sage might argue, though, that he is not responsible for his players demonstrating a lack of basic brainpower.

Jean-Philippe Mateta receives his first red card for Crystal Palace! 🟥 https://t.co/U9UYb29mbk.

All of this was welcomed heartily by the Spurs fans, who celebrated Mateta’s dismissal as though it was a goal. Recent results have restored some of the enthusiasm in this corner of north London and the mood here was buoyant, even before Gray’s opener.

Sources indicate that “Now we are playing as a team,” De Zerbi mentioned. “Before the international break, we were playing as many good players but not as a team. We demonstrated our maturity. We are improving.”.

The second goal was always coming and it arrived in the 73rd minute, when Van Hecke attacked a wonderful cross by Mateus Fernandes. Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson saved the first attempt but the ball dropped onto the head of Van Hecke, now seated in the six-yard box, and he happily nodded it home.

It has been revealed that jan Paul van Hecke doubles Spurs' lead! 👊 https://t.co/1Odkkr8wBJ.

In a recent development, the latest signings at Spurs endured a difficult first few weeks but there were more signs here that they are adjusting to De Zerbi’s system. Sandro Tonali was exceptional in midfield and teenage talent Luca Williams-Barnett also sparkled off the bench. “Tonali was unbelievable,” De Zerbi stated. “We played with two players more: Tonali was double.”.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”.

In a recent development, palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

The visitors are without the injured trio of Ismaila Sarr, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chadi Riad, but there’s hope that Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen are fit to be involved this evening after they both missed the Fulham victory.

Ngumoha was in superb form for Liverpool as they beat Man Utd 4-0, and it’s fair to say it was a pretty easy game for the Reds, with plenty of chances for an even bigger score-line.

Speaking after the game, the 18-year-old sounded delighted to shine in this significant game, admitting that it’s special to score and assist at such a young age against Liverpool’s rivals.

In a recent development, “Games like Liverpool-United can’t really get much bigger in my eyes. To get the three points here at Anfield is special. It was a really notable game today,” Ngumoha said in his post-match interview, as quoted by BBC Sport.

Sources indicate that on possibly scoring more against the Red Devils, he added: “Sometimes when we are two goals up we can get a big complacent really. Sources indicate that “As fans they always want us to score chances and we know we should have scored more. Creating those chances is important as well. It’s about keeping a cool head and keeping composed and they will come.”.

In a recent development, frosinone coach Massimiliano Alvini explains his surprising transformation to take on Ruben Amorim’s Milan. ‘It is a different strategy, but the principles remain the same.’.

It kicks off at San Siro at 17.00 GMT (18.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s five Serie A games on the Liveblog.

Star striker Antonio Raimondo is still out with a sprained ankle, along with Florian Grillitsch, while Gabriele Bracaglia is suspended.

Rather than using Daniel Birligea as the centre-forward, Frosinone appear to have shifted from a 4-2-3-1 formation to 3-4-3 with Romano Schmid as the False 9.

“The players at your disposal is everything, because they are the ones on the pitch,” Alvini told Sky Sport Italia and DAZN Italia.

“We decided to push Milan as far as possible, to give few reference points, to always be moving forward. It is a different strategy today, but the principles remain the same, to run forward with defenders rather than have the midfielders back-tracking. We are aware of what awaits us, we’ll try to have our game.”.

While some sources had Giorgio Kvernadze as the False 9, and others picked Fares Ghedjemis, Alvini confirmed it is Austrian midfielder Schmid who has that position.

“Schmid is the centre-forward, Monterisi is in central defence,” he confessed.

That suggests it is a three-man defence, the first time all season that Frosinone have taken this approach.

The Canarini go into this game in sixth place, just behind Milan in fifth, and have been a massive surprise since earning promotion from Serie B last season.

“Milan are one of the teams who pass out from the back the most, so we’ll try to keep our ideas and put them into action, that is all. We come here to play, not to look around and admire the atmosphere,” added Alvini.

“I’m pleased for the lads that they feel ambitious, we must have the right attitude and take the game to them.”.

What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1276 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.
  • The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.
  • Sources indicate that "We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner announced after the talks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.

The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.

Sources indicate that "We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner announced after the talks. US envoys Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow on Thursday, where they are due to meet President Vladimir Putin.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had earlier suggested an exchange of "1,000 for 1,000" prisoners, or "1,500 for 1,500." Russia remarked a large-scale prisoner exchange with Ukraine could take place within the next two to three weeks.

Following the meetings, Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram that the parties had discussed security guarantees and that "the first step should be ending this war and ensuring Ukraine's security." He also stressed that Europe should be involved "at every stage of genuine diplomacy.".

Experts interviewed by DW agree that the main outcome of the talks is humanitarian.

"The agreement on a prisoner exchange is already a major step forward," says Artjom Bronzhukov of the Ukrainian think tank Polityka.

It has been revealed that pavlo Lakiychuk of the Ukrainian Center for Global Studies Strategy XXI also viewed it as a "very tangible result." He told DW that "getting our people back is already a major success. That is why it is worth continuing.".

A real breakthrough, he added, would be the release of civilian detainees from territories occupied since 2014, particularly people from Crimea, who have been held in Russian prisons for years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Davyd Arakhamia, head of the ruling Servant of the People parliamentary faction and Ukraine's representative at the talks in Abu Dhabi, gave a positive assessment of the trilateral talks with the US and Russia, expressing hope that an agreement could be reached by the end of the year.

"I think the Russians came with extremely strict instructions, and it was difficult to ease the tone of the discussion. But the way the US representatives structured the talks with a view to the postwar situation in both countries opened up a dialogue, in my opinion, and allowed us to work together more productively," Arakhamia stated at a joint press conference with US and Ukrainian representatives following the talks.

Iuliia Osmolovska of the Kyiv office of the international think tank GLOBSEC cautions against reading too much into the positive assessments of the talks from Washington and Kyiv.

Recent findings suggest that "Diplomats taking part in negotiations will never say that everything went badly and that they have no expectations. Even when no results are achieved, they will still emphasize that the talks were constructive," she remarked. "For anyone familiar with diplomatic language, these are simply standard phrases.".

In a recent development, osmolovska points to a joint assessment by 71 Ukrainian security and defense experts published by GLOBSEC in the summer. According to the assessment, the chances of a peace agreement or at least a ceasefire being reached this year or next stand at just 19%.

She blames this on the fact that neither side is "ready" for genuine negotiations. Russia, in particular, has yet to accept that its objectives cannot be achieved by military means. "What we are seeing now is more of a farce, an attempt by all sides to put a brave face on things and create the impression that something is moving forward," Osmolovska said.

Artjom Bronzhukov sees the talks as a way for Moscow to buy time.

"The visits by the Russian delegation, particularly under the leadership of Vladimir Medinsky, are nothing more than an attempt to stall and sell empty promises to the US administration in the form of grand agreements, in order to continue receiving so-called gestures of goodwill from Washington, such as the lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel," the political scientist says.

According to recent reports, ahead of the talks, several Western media outlets reported on latest US proposals concerning disputed territories. The Economist, for example, reported on a proposal to redraw the administrative boundaries of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions. However, a member of the Ukrainian delegation stressed that there had "never been any discussion of concessions on territories occupied by Russia.".

Washington made no official comment on the reports.

Kyrylo Budanov, a member of the negotiating delegation and head of the Ukrainian president's office, declined to say whether Russia had used the talks to demand that Ukrainian troops withdraw from the Donbas. Asked by journalists whether Moscow was still insisting that Ukraine pull out of the region, Budanov stated the content of the negotiations would remain confidential until an agreement was reached.

In a recent development, "The issues discussed in the talks are matters for negotiation. The only thing that matters is the outcome. Once we achieve it, it will be made public," Budanov remarked.

The head of the Russian delegation, Vladimir Medinsky, took a different tone, declaring that "every inch of our land will be returned to Russia one way or another." He was responding to reports in European media that Ukraine was rejecting territorial concessions.

In addition to the Crimean Peninsula, annexed in 2014, Russian President Vladimir Putin claims the four Ukrainian regions of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson in their entirety as Russian territory, even though Russia does not have full military control over them.

"Putin is not fighting over villages and ruined cowsheds in the Donbas. He is fighting for geopolitical influence and trying to exploit the collapse of the old world order," says Artjom Bronzhukov.

Recent findings suggest that the expert from the Polityka think tank recalls that Ukraine was already asked in early 2026 to withdraw its troops from the part of the Donbas it controls and turn the area into a free economic zone. Such a zone "would very rapidly become a Russian-controlled area," he warns.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pavlo Lakiychuk questions the idea of changing administrative boundaries.

According to recent reports, "Why would Putin stop there?" asks the expert from the Strategy XXI center. In his view, US negotiators are seeking to extract unilateral concessions from Ukraine "step by step" without demanding anything in return from Russia.

Iuliia Osmolovska describes the proposal as "very original," but says it would pose risks for Ukraine's leadership. Even if the Ukrainian delegation agreed to it, which Osmolovska doubts, the decision would have to be explained to the public, which, she says, is not ready to accept it.

The GLOBSEC expert points out that, following the last harsh winter, marked by shortages of electricity and heating, only 5% of Ukrainians were willing to make concessions to Russia in exchange for an end to attacks on the energy sector.

Following the meeting between Jared Kushner, US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Putin in Moscow, Volodymyr Zelenskyy mentioned he wants to "coordinate positions with the Americans once again." No further trilateral meetings have been revealed so far.

It has been revealed that iuliia Osmolovska believes the parties will sooner or later have to admit that the negotiations have reached a dead end. She expects each side to return to military action.

Pavlo Lakiychuk, by contrast, believes the talks should continue, if only to secure the return of prisoners. He is also convinced that Europeans "will always be there," because the matter is not just the Russian-Ukrainian war but the security of the entire continent.

This article was originally published in Ukrainian.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leny Yoro's sending off in Manchester United's 4-0 defeat to Liverpool came in controversial fashion, and VAR expert Dale Johnson has weighed in on whether referee Sam Barrott got the decision right.

Regardless of the red card, this was a pitiful performance from United and the worst possible start for Mauricio Pochettino. He watched his side capitulate within eight minutes when Matthijs de Ligt, strangely handed a start, got caught out and Yoro raced back before barging into Alexander Isak.

Sources indicate that yoro sent Isak to the turf just outside the box, and Barrott deemed this to have been a red card offence due to the French defender being the last man. Most United fans aren't using the dismissal as an excuse for their team's fifth league defeat of the season, but many are questioning whether the challenge warranted such punishment.

It has been revealed that isak was played through on goal and the Liverpool striker took a heavy touch, sending the ball a fair distance away from him when Yoro made the challenge. VAR didn't feel the need to intervene and potentially downgrade the red card to a caution.

Johnson delved into Barrott's decision and explained that the referee had four key considerations to make over Yoro denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity. These are "the distance between the offence and the goal", "the general direction of play", "the likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball" and "the location and number of defenders and attackers".

Three of those factors were satisfied because Isak ran directly towards goal in a central position and United had no covering defender. The main question is the "likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball".

In a recent development, united will argue that Yoro's contact came after Isak's touch and therefore there is no case that the challenge caused the player to over-run the ball. Johnson suggested in his BBC Sport article that Barrott and VAR John Brooks had to assess whether Isak would definitely have got to the ball ahead of goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Sources indicate that johnson added: "And that if he had, it would have been a good scoring chance. If there is any doubt, then it should not be a red card. It is a borderline case, and as such the VAR would not be expected to intervene for a clear and obvious error.".

It has been revealed that united were put to the sword thereafter when Dominik Szoboszlai scored the opener with the resulting free-kick (10'). Florian Wirtz added a second (13') before Rio Ngumoha (66') and Victor Munoz (83') sealed an emphatic victory for Andoni Iraola's men.

Recent findings suggest that there were differing opinions on the red card amongst Sky Sports pundits as United legends Gary Neville and Roy Keane disagreed. Neville defended Barrott's decision and tore into Yoro for a "clumsy" challenge and "poor anticipation".

In a recent development, keane, however, felt Yoro could feel hard done by. He was "amazed" to see De Ligt fail to read the flight of the ball, arguing that Isak's heavy touch meant he wasn't going to regain possession:.

"Isak has done well, but I actually don't think he's going to get the ball... He's not getting the ball. There's no way he's getting the ball. It's clumsy from United, it's one straight ball over the top. You shouldn't be in so much trouble, but there's no way he's getting that ball. Absolutely not.".

Recent findings suggest that this is the second time this season Yoro has been sent off, compounding a miserable afternoon for United. Their loss to Liverpool leaves them sitting 19th after 11 games played, and they will be without the Frenchman for Brentford's visit to Old Trafford on Saturday unless they successfully appeal the decision.

#60090. Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (821 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA), a firm would have to remind you before the free trial ends and get your explicit agreement before it can start charging you.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Commission presented the proposal on Wednesday.
  • "We haven't seen that kind of reform in consumer protection in the last 20 years," Agustin Reyna, director general of the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), told DW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA), a firm would have to remind you before the free trial ends and get your explicit agreement before it can start charging you. The proposed law would also make it easier to cancel a subscription online and require reminders before certain contracts renew automatically.

Recent findings suggest that the Commission presented the proposal on Wednesday. It wants to give consumers more control over how much time and money they spend online.

"We haven't seen that kind of reform in consumer protection in the last 20 years," Agustin Reyna, director general of the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), told DW.

Sources indicate that his organization pushed for stronger EU rules against manipulative online practices. He sees the proposal as a good starting point for tackling problems that frustrate consumers every day.

The proposal also includes a ban on manipulative marketing tactics, so-called "dark patterns." A concrete example: You are trying to reserve a hotel room and the website claims that only three are left, a potentially false claim to pressure you into buying.

According to recent reports, A concert ticket that gets more expensive while you're waiting in an online queue raises a different problem. The price could still go up in the process, but the seller would have to show the current price while you wait and tell you the maximum you could be asked to pay.

Sources indicate that online games that encourage customers to spend their money to advance are also targeted. Children would no longer be able to pay to win or get to the next level of their online game.

Recent findings suggest that marketing and personalized ads would need to be clearly marked and restricted in the case of children. Consumers should get the option to switch off doomscrolling functions such as the autoplay of videos, showing one clip after the other. With these latest rules, the EU wants to make apps and websites less addictive.

For Christoph Busch, an academic with a focus on consumer law and digital services based at Osnabrück University in Germany, the option to opt out doesn't go far enough. He argues that a version in which consumers actively have to choose to opt into those functions would be more effective.

"But then there is always the question of proportionality," Busch noted. "And I think here the European legislators are trying to balance different interests.".

These competing interests are particularly visible in the gaming industry, where interest groups have warned that the proposed EU restrictions could hurt developers and leave players with fewer options to choose from.

Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation called the proposal "unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate," arguing that a ban on selling children features that help them win or advance is worded so broadly that it "could cover almost any purchase in a game.".

It has been revealed that for Busch, this argument doesn't hold. "If your business model is based on addictive design features, then maybe your business model has to be reviewed," he said.

Catalina Goanta, an associate professor of private law and technology at Utrecht University, emphasized in an interview with DW that "regulation can very easily slide into overregulation.".

Even though she believes that the DFA is a solid and reasonable compromise, she argues that prohibiting dark patterns and doomscrolling altogether would be too prohibitive. Many of the complications consumers presently face could be resolved by enforcing existing regulation more effectively, she stated.

She points to the fact that the EU has made a name for itself in the past by adding new rules and regulations that have made it more difficult to access the European market, especially for small online businesses.

BEUC director Agustin Reyna disagrees.

"Instead of having 27 different regulations to adhere to, companies will now only get one," Reyna said.

For him, this speaks for simplification, especially when the responsibility for compliance is shared between online influencers and the platforms they publish on.

According to the newly introduced legislation, the EU would have the possibility to impose fines of up to six percent of a company's global annual revenue should the company violate the law.

The European Parliament and the Council, which represents member state governments, still have to agree on the text and formally adopt it. All experts agree that in that process, changes are still very likely.

Recent findings suggest that "It will be a difficult trialogue, especially in this climate of simplification and deregulation with a focus on strengthening European competitiveness," said Christoph Busch. In that climate, it is not easy to add consumer rights, he adds.

In a recent development, agustin Reyna is more optimistic. "The parliament is a divided house, much more than in the past," he notes. "But consumer protection is a subject that brings parties together because it brings tangible outcomes to people.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of crucial saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

Alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

Zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! 🫨 https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk.

“I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager said. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

According to recent reports, “I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

“We have to change our mind promptly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”.

Villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

Recent findings suggest that it was awarded after Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header hit Sander Berge’s raised hand. Nobody appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor by VAR to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

According to recent reports, mcGinn’s attempt, however, hit the crossbar and the chance to take an early lead went begging. The Villa captain seemed a strange choice to take the spot-kick as he has only ever scored one career penalty, but Emery defended the choice, saying: “We analysed the penalty takers in the squad and it was McGinn here.”.

Of all the daft statements to have come out of Aston Villa – and I am including Doug Ellis’s frequent claims that he invented the bicycle kick – it is hard to think of anything as absurd as suing a pundit for speaking the truth.

Jamie Carragher’s common-sense declaration that Villa manager Unai Emery might consider a move to Manchester United – because it is a bigger club – has apparently inflicted such a deep wound to the self-esteem of Nassef Sawiris, the chairman, that he has initiated a legal complaint.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If there was any doubt over the scale of the task facing Mauricio Pochettino at Old Trafford, a social media exchange between one of his players and a content creator has illustrated it perfectly.
  • Manchester United winger Amad Diallo responded directly to an Instagram account criticising his recent display.
  • “Just shut your mouth, bro - you’re talking too much now,” Diallo wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If there was any doubt over the scale of the task facing Mauricio Pochettino at Old Trafford, a social media exchange between one of his players and a content creator has illustrated it perfectly.

Manchester United winger Amad Diallo responded directly to an Instagram account criticising his recent display.

“Just shut your mouth, bro - you’re talking too much now,” Diallo wrote. “Go play in my place if it bothers you that much”.

While it is understandable for a young player to feel the weight of fan frustration, the optics of the situation are poor.

A Manchester United player reacting publicly to a troll on social media just days before a upcoming manager takes charge is an indictment of the dressing room’s current mental state.

🚨📲 𝗡𝗘𝗪: Amad Diallo’s comment on a fan who criticized him: “Just shut your mouth, bro—you’re talking too much now. Go play in my place if it bothers you that much.” https://t.co/sLqd3B912HNovember 18, 2026.

The incoming Pochettino will want an emotionally resilient squad, given the responsibility of representing one of the biggest clubs in world football.

This incident highlights the repair job required at Carrington, because if a highly-rated 24-year-old is spending his free time scrolling through his own mentions and biting back at criticism, it begs a much larger, more worrying question: Are all Manchester United players this hyper-aware of their online reception?

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

If they are, it explains a great deal about the fragility on display during matches. A squad that lives and dies by its social media mentions is unequipped to handle the pressure cooker environment that is Old Trafford.

When things go wrong on the pitch - and they frequently do for this current iteration of Man United - players affected by outside noise are far more likely to retreat into their shells than rally together.

Pochettino’s first priority therefore cannot be tactical; it must be cultural. He has to insulate his squad from the news cycle which bounces between online praise and vitriol. The Argentine could do a lot worse than instituting a bunker mentality from day one at Old Trafford.

Joe joined FourFourTwo as senior digital writer in July 2025 after five years covering Leeds United in the Championship and Premier League. Joe's 'Mastermind' specialist subject is 2000s-era Newcastle United having had a season ticket at St. James' Park for 10 years before relocating to Leeds and later London. Joe takes a keen interest in youth football, covering PL2, U21 Euros, as well as U20 and U17 World Cups in the past, in addition to hosting the industry-leading football recruitment-focused SCOUTED podcast. He is also one of the lucky few to have 'hit top bins' as a contestant on Soccer AM. It wasn't a shin-roller.

EU leaders tussle over whom to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks

💡 Key Takeaways
  • European leaders are under pressure to put forward a name to represent them in Ukraine peace talks after US envoy Steve Witkoff told reporters that the Europeans will be present at the next meetings.
  • When asked by DW during the European Political Community summit in Dublin why Europe should only get one seat at the table while the US gets two, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas responded with a wry, ironic laugh ― clearly a sign of the frustration felt by European leaders about being sidelined thus far.
  • The summit of 47 European leaders in Dublin comes in the wake of a diplomatic tour by two Donald Trump administration advisers, the president's son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, to talks in Abu Dhabi, followed by a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European leaders are under pressure to put forward a name to represent them in Ukraine peace talks after US envoy Steve Witkoff told reporters that the Europeans will be present at the next meetings.

When asked by DW during the European Political Community summit in Dublin why Europe should only get one seat at the table while the US gets two, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas responded with a wry, ironic laugh ― clearly a sign of the frustration felt by European leaders about being sidelined thus far.

The summit of 47 European leaders in Dublin comes in the wake of a diplomatic tour by two Donald Trump administration advisers, the president's son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, to talks in Abu Dhabi, followed by a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.

The pair then hot-footed their way to Dublin to debrief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelekenskyy.

Zelenskyy and Kushner also said Thursday that Europeans would be at the table for the next talks with Russia on ending the war.

According to recent reports, kallas is one of the figures tipped as most likely to represent the EU in any future talks to end Russia's war against Ukraine, alongside EU Council President Antonio Costa. As yet, the EU hasn’t been able to land on one central figure to send ― many of the national leaders want to be present themselves.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz insisted Europe will be present.

"At the table must be sitting Ukraine, must be sitting the Europeans, must be sitting the Americans, and naturally Russia," he told reporters in Dublin.

But he, like many other leaders, played down the idea of appointing a special envoy for the talks.

Zelenskyy is insistent on European involvement in the peace talks.

"Not directly yet, and not yet when the Russians are at the table," he told the other leaders during the Dublin meetings. "But Europeans are already involved. And we need to make sure that Europe becomes a regular part of these negotiations.".

Sources indicate that europe’s division over exactly who should be present has caused a public battle to erupt. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote an excoriating letter to Costa last week, bemoaning the lack of unity.

"By projecting the image of a Europe that is in disarray, we are merely serving the interests of those who want this war to continue," wrote Meloni.

European leaders had even seemed divided over their level of frustration about the situation.

Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Jansa said in Dublin that it was creating a "bad mood" among leaders, however Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs disputed those comments saying, "I don’t feel that.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The palpable fear among the leaders in Dublin is that the US will accept Russia's demands that Europe changes the way it structures its own security, mainly through the NATO military alliance, in exchange for a seat at the table.

Putin stated a commitment that Ukraine will never join NATO and even the potential rolling back of the alliance to remove latest joiners Finland and Sweden, could be among his demands.

Recent findings suggest that "What do we hear from them [Europeans]?" asked Putin during the meeting with Kushner and Witkoff in Moscow. "That once a peace agreement is signed, they will immediately deploy troops in Ukraine. This is a legitimate target for us, so the war will resume immediately.".

This is exactly the kind of rhetoric the European leaders say they are most wary of, especially those in Russia’s direct neighborhood.

Recent findings suggest that "Right now, we are in the [Russian] trap," noted Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal. "If something is a threat to you, will you discuss your defense with the threat [itself]?".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US President Donald Trump remarked publicly that he was hoping for a "very significant, beautiful agreement" that "might involve all of Europe.".

Zelensky remarked he found the US approach "a bit strange.".

Many of Europe's leaders speaking in Dublin referenced previous agreements with Russia that they believe Moscow has breached.

They include the 1975 Helsinki Accords, the 1990 Paris Charter, 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act and the one they consider most notable: the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, which forbids Russia from using force against Ukraine unless in self-defense.

The rancor over the seat at the peace talks is drawing focus away from arguably the bigger battle in the EU now ― how to fund Ukraine as the war continues.

Back in October, the European Commission identified a €70 billion hole in the EU’s funding it had promised for Ukraine’s economy.

Slovakia’s Prime Minister Robert Fico has opposed any further financial and military support for Ukraine.

But Germany's Merz warned he could block the EU's next seven-year budget unless member states agree to contribute to Ukraine's financing.
